title: Apple fined $15.5 million as South Korea orders changes to App Store rules
snippet: Apple and Google were fined today in South Korea over their app payment practices, with regulators also ordering both companies to change several policies. Here are the details. more…
fullText:
Apple and Google were fined today in South Korea over their app payment practices, with regulators also ordering both companies to change several policies. Here are the details.

Apple’s App Store woes keep mounting

South Korea’s Korea Media and Communications Commission (KMCC) announced today a series of fines and corrective orders against Apple and Google over violations of the country’s Telecommunications Business Act.

Specifically for Apple, the KMCC imposed a fine of 20.81 billion won (approximately $15.5 million) and ordered the company to revise its App Store policies regarding payment methods and app review procedures, as well as prevent what it referred to as “discriminatory commission” practices from recurring.

In its announcement, the KMCC noted:

This is the first enforcement case under the 2021 amendment to the Telecommunications Business Act, which introduced prohibited acts for app market operators, such as forcing specific payment methods and unfairly delaying app reviews.

In essence, the decision centers around three violations: forcing specific payment methods, unfairly delaying app reviews, and imposing discriminatory commissions.

On the payment methods front, the KMCC said Apple and Google “effectively forced” developers to use their own in-app payment systems by imposing a 26% commission and additional restrictions on third-party alternatives.

“This constitutes an act in which an app market operator unfairly uses its position in transactions to force mobile content providers and others to use a specific payment method,” the KMCC said.

As a result, Apple and Google must revise their policies to allow external payment methods and address restrictions imposed on developers using alternative payment systems.

As for the app review process, the KMCC found that Apple and Google “delayed app reviews, for example by not providing specific reasons when reviews were delayed or not clearly responding to individual inquiries about the reasons for delays and expected timelines.”

Accordingly, Apple and Google must revise their app review procedures to address these issues.

Finally, on the discriminatory commissions, which applied only to Apple, the KMCC found that between July 2015 and January 2023, the company calculated its 30% commission differently for South Korean and overseas developers. While overseas developers were charged based on prices excluding value-added tax (VAT), South Korean developers were charged based on prices including VAT.

“KMCC determined that this constituted an act of unfairly providing rates, numbers, telecommunications facilities, or other economic benefits for telecommunications services or bundled services in a discriminatory manner compared to other users […].”

The KMCC said Apple will also have to take measures to prevent discriminatory commission practices between South Korean and overseas developers from recurring.

According to Reuters, Apple said it “‌disagreed ⁠with the decision and was evaluating options in accordance with South Korean ​laws.” ​Apple added that “⁠it has worked with outside developers ​to enable innovation ​through ⁠its App Store.”

Today’s decision comes on the heels of similar regulatory pressure in other markets, including Brazil and Japan, where Apple has introduced alternative app distribution and payment options in response to local competition rules.

The company has also faced years of scrutiny in the European Union, where it recently overhauled its App Store fees and business terms to address concerns raised by the European Commission.

title: iOS 27.2 introduces new age verification feature using selfie
snippet: iOS 27.2 is here, and it introduces a new feature for age verification using a selfie. Here are the details. more…
fullText:
iOS 27.2 is here, and it introduces a new feature for age verification using a selfie. Here are the details.

Apple offers new, privacy-focused way to verify your age in iOS 27.2

An increasing number of territories around the world now require iPhone age verification in certain scenarios, such as when creating an Apple Account, updating your software, downloading apps, or changing select settings.

Per Apple, these requirements may apply to users in Australia, Brazil, Singapore, South Korea, the UK, and also the United States (Texas).

While iOS already offered other methods of age verification, such as using a credit card or scanning your ID, iOS 27.2 adds a new option: taking a selfie.

Per a new support document, Apple says:

In some states, countries, or regions, you might be asked to confirm that you’re an adult before you can take certain actions on your Apple Account. One way to confirm that you’re an adult is to take a selfie. An age-estimation model will then evaluate the images of your face.

The selfie option isn’t available in all regions, but if you’re asked to confirm you’re an adult, you might see the option to use a selfie. 

Here’s how it works per Apple’s instructions:

Choose the option to take a selfie, then tap Get Started.

Hold your device in front of you and center your face in the frame.

Capture all four angles of your face by moving your head slowly right, left, up, and down. Follow the onscreen guidance to complete confirmation. It might take a moment to estimate your age.

Apple says your privacy is protected by its age-estimation models running both on-device and on Private Cloud Compute. The selfie “isn’t accessible to anyone, not even Apple.” And after your age has been confirmed, the selfie is deleted immediately and “isn’t retained in any form.”

To learn more about Apple’s new age verification feature in iOS 27.2, read the full support document here.

Have you ever had to perform age verification on your iPhone? How did the process go? Let us know in the comments.

title: New M6 Macs buck Apple’s second wave of price hikes
snippet: In addition to the spec bumps, today’s M6-powered iMac and 14-inch MacBook Pro announcements came with an extra piece of good news: prices remained unchanged from the previous generations, unlike several other recent Apple product launches that brought another round of increases. Here are the details. more…
fullText:
In addition to the spec bumps, today’s M6-powered iMac and 14-inch MacBook Pro announcements came with an extra piece of good news: prices remained unchanged from the previous generations, unlike several other recent Apple product launches that brought another round of increases. Here are the details.

Prices unchanged, for a change

Earlier today, Apple announced two new M6-powered Macs, which start at the same prices as their predecessors.

And while both models benefit from the faster M6 chip, iMac buyers are also getting more CPU and GPU cores for the same price, as the base model now comes with a 10-core CPU and 10-core GPU, up from the 8-core CPU and 8-core GPU in the previous generation’s M4 chip.

As 9to5Mac readers probably remember, Apple raised prices across much of its product lineup in June, including the iMac, which went from $1,299 to $1,499, and the 14-inch MacBook Pro, which went from $1,699 to $1,999.

At the time, the company also hiked prices for the HomePod mini, Apple TV 4K, and iPad mini, all of which saw new versions announced recently with yet another price bump.

The HomePod mini, which went from $99 to $129 in June, now costs $149 with the second-generation model. The Apple TV 4K, which previously started at $129, jumped to $199 in June, while the new generation starts at $299 (albeit with twice the storage). And the iPad mini, which went from $499 to $599 in June, now starts at $699 with the OLED model announced earlier this week.

And while iPhone prices were left untouched during the June increases, that changed in September with the launch of the iPhone 18 Pro and iPhone 18 Pro Max, which now start at $1,199 and $1,299, respectively, up $100 from their predecessors.

Apple also raised prices by $100 for the older iPhone models still in its lineup, including the iPhone 17, iPhone Air, and iPhone 17e.

	

With that in mind, although the new M6-powered Macs are far from cheap, it’s still good news that they didn’t come with another price hike on top of the June increases.

Things are looking way less promising for those waiting for tomorrow’s expected OLED touchscreen MacBook Pro models, however, with Bloomberg reporting that Apple has discussed a $2,899 starting price for the 14-inch model. If Apple applies the same rumored $400 premium to the current 16-inch model, which starts at $2,999, the new version could cost $3,399 or more.

That, in turn, makes Apple’s decision to keep prices unchanged for today’s M6-powered Macs all the more welcome, especially for buyers who were already dreading the possibility of having to shell out even more after waiting for the new models. Whether that will hold remains to be seen.

What’s your take on Apple’s pricing strategy for the M6 Macs announced earlier today? Let us know in the comments.

title: Last-minute leak reveals new touchscreen MacBook Pro details: pricing, new cooling system, more
snippet: In a roundup of what to expect from tomorrow’s “Pro and Tell” event, Bloomberg’s Mark Gurman shared new details about the upcoming OLED touchscreen MacBook Pro models. Here’s what to expect. more…
fullText:
In a roundup of what to expect from tomorrow’s “Pro and Tell” event, Bloomberg’s Mark Gurman shared new details about the upcoming OLED touchscreen MacBook Pro models. Here’s what to expect.

Report reveals last-minute details and backstory of rumored touchscreen MacBook Pro

Tomorrow, Apple is expected to announce its first-ever touchscreen MacBook Pro models, featuring OLED displays, Dynamic Island, and a thinner, lighter design.

While previous reports have suggested that the new models will come with significantly higher prices, Bloomberg now offers more specific figures, along with additional details about their redesign.

According to Gurman’s sources, “Apple has discussed charging $2,899 for the new 14-inch model with an M5 Pro chip,” which, if Apple applies at least the same $400 premium to the 16-inch model, would mean “the new version will cost at least $3,399.”

Compared to the $2,199 and $2,699 starting prices of the 14-inch and 16-inch M5 Pro MacBook Pro models before Apple’s June price hikes, that would represent an increase of at least $700 in just four months.

Gurman added that “Apple plans to continue selling the non-touch versions alongside the new machines,” and further commented on that in a post on X:

I do not expect the current non-touch MacBook Pros (14 inch at $2499 and 16-inch at $2999) to go anywhere tomorrow. Retail stores are fully stocked up on those as well still. https://t.co/UTs2NJ1N3A

— Mark Gurman (@markgurman) October 27, 2026

In other words, he expects the new OLED touchscreen MacBook Pro models to sit at the top of Apple’s current laptop lineup, rather than replacing the existing M5 Pro and M5 Max models.

However, users looking to get the redesigned hardware will likely have to pay the premium, regardless of whether they actually want a touchscreen.

At $2,899, the 14-inch model would mark the highest starting price for a new MacBook Pro model, surpassing the $2,799 Apple charged for a 17-inch version introduced in 2006. The pricing would also put Apple among the most expensive makers of touch-screen laptops, alongside premium offerings from Dell Technologies Inc. that also feature OLED displays.

Beyond the OLED touchscreen, Gurman reaffirmed that the new MacBook Pro models will feature a slightly thinner design, thinner bezels, a noticeably lighter body, and a redesigned hinge to prevent the screen from moving when touched, all of which we covered earlier today here.

The report also adds a new detail: Apple has reworked the cooling system to improve airflow through the hinge while helping reduce the computers’ weight.

	

Finally, Gurman’s report offers some behind-the-scenes details about how Apple decided to bring touchscreens to the Mac. According to his sources, Tim Cook greenlit the touchscreen MacBook Pro project roughly four years ago, in part because the feature had become one of the most requested by Apple customers.

“He said we should just do it,” according to a person with knowledge of the decision.

Gurman added that Ternus oversaw development of the new MacBook Pro models. According to the report, Ternus believed “Apple had fallen behind in the area and indicated internally that touch screens had become table stakes for laptops, making it time for the company to embrace the technology.”

According to the report, Apple plans to open preorders for the new touchscreen MacBook Pro models tomorrow, October 28, with availability potentially beginning as early as November 6, alongside the new M6-powered Macs announced today.

title: Apple releases iOS 27.2, here’s what’s new
snippet: Apple has officially released iOS 27.2 for iPhone. The update brings a new look to Apple Music, more Siri AI languages, changes to Messages and Podcasts, and Apple Pencil support for iPhone Duo. Here’s what’s new. more…
fullText:
Apple has officially released iOS 27.2 for iPhone. The update brings a new look to Apple Music, more Siri AI languages, changes to Messages and Podcasts, and Apple Pencil support for iPhone Duo. Here’s what’s new.

Release notes

Siri AI (All iPhone 16 models and later, iPhone 15 Pro, iPhone 15 Pro Max)

Siri AI can recall your past conversations, so you can ask Siri about something it told you before, like the restaurants it recommended last week

Siri AI can draw from more sources to give you a great answer, including photos attached in Messages, Calendar event attendees, your voicemails, and better results from Safari history and Reading List

Excluded Apps lets you choose which apps Siri, Search, and suggestions can access, all from one setting

Granular text selection lets you select and copy just the part of a Siri response you need

Siri AI is available in more languages, with support for French, Japanese, Korean, Portuguese, and Spanish. Siri AI is not available in the EU or mainland China

Other

Suggestions in Messages help you take action based on the context of your conversations, like adding a Calendar invite for a dinner

Shared Albums in Photos adds the ability to edit captions and comments, to avoid adding duplicate photos, and can display a reminder before albums expire so participants can save important photos and videos

Support for SynthID watermarking to help identify whether an image was generated or modified with generative tools in Photos and Image Playground

The Home tab in the Podcasts app offers two separate sections for New Episodes and Continue Playing, letting you find the latest updates from your shows and then pick up where you left off

Friends tab in the Games app provides context on friend suggestions and shows recent games played on friends’ player pages

Simple Profiles in the Apple TV app lets everyone in your household have their own profile, with recommendations that fit what they like to watch

FaceTime supports adding a third party sign language interpreter or live captioner to a call

Here’s what we’ve seen from testing as well.

Apple Pencil support for iPhone Duo

iPhone Duo gains support for Apple Pencil with iOS 27.2. Apple originally announced the feature as coming later this year, and it’s arriving with this update.

There is one detail to keep in mind: iPhone Duo works with Apple Pencil (USB-C). Apple Pencil Pro and other Pencil models aren’t supported. More on Apple Pencil support.

Apple Music gets a new look

Apple Music has a new black-and-white app icon that replaces the familiar red design. Inside the app, blue replaces red as the accent color for the selected tab. Apple has also refreshed Music widgets with black backgrounds. More on the Apple Music changes.

Messages, Podcasts, and Apple TV updates

Messages gains Suggested Actions, which offer shortcuts based on the conversation. A message about plans, for example, can include an option to create a calendar event or reminder. Settings also lets you control which types of suggestions appear.

Apple Podcasts separates new episodes from episodes you’ve already started. New Episodes and Continue Playing give each category its own place on the Home tab.

The Apple TV app also adds profiles on iPhone, letting users keep their viewing history and recommendations separate. More on the app updates.

More Siri AI languages and Group FaceTime Dual Capture

Siri AI adds support for French, Japanese, Korean, Portuguese, and Spanish.

Meanwhile, Dual Capture expands to Group FaceTime. The feature lets you share views from the front and rear cameras simultaneously. More on these additions.

New Home controls

The Home app adds Lock After Closing and Door Left Open options for compatible smart locks. These let you automatically lock a door after it closes or receive an alert if it stays open too long. More on the smart lock features.

HomePod owners also gain a Lock Controls setting after updating both their iPhone and HomePod to 27.2. This prevents unwanted taps from starting audio, while preserving touch responses for features like timers and alarms. More on HomePod Lock Controls.

What about the new Health app?

Apple’s redesigned Health app appeared in earlier iOS 27.2 betas, but Apple removed it before release. The upgrade is still planned for later this year. More on the Health app release timing.

You can install iOS 27.2 by opening Settings > General > Software Update on your iPhone.

title: Apple launches its new touchscreen MacBook Pro
snippet: Apple's new touchscreen MacBook Pro starts at $2,899.
fullText:
After years of resisting, Apple today launched a MacBook Pro with a touchscreen starting at $2,899. The release comes nearly 10 years after the company first tried integrating touchscreens on its laptops, with its Touch Bar on a MacBook Pro, which it later went on to remove.

The new MacBook Pro more fully embraces the touchscreen, offering a new PROLED XDR Display in both 14-inch and 16-inch screen sizes. The device is powered by M5 Pro and M5 Max chips as options to choose from, along with up to 128GB of unified memory and up to 16TB of storage. The display has 2,000 nits peak HDR and SDR brightness and a 10,000,000:1 contrast ratio.

To make the new MacBook easy to use, Apple designed a hinge that stabilizes the screen when users touch it. This also helps to stabilize the camera when you are on a video call and trying to access content on the display.

In addition, the screen will include a Dynamic Island-style cutout instead of the notch that’s present on most of the current MacBooks. Plus, the new MacBook features a six-speaker array with a new woofer design for better sound.

The 14-inch Pro weighs 3.0 pounds (1.38 kg), and the 16-inch Pro weighs 4.0 pounds (1.82 kg) — lighter than its non-touch predecessors.

Both feature three Thunderbolt 5 ports, an HDMI port, an SDXC card slot, MagSafe, and a headphone jack. Users can hook up three external displays on the M5 Pro variant and up to four displays on the M5 Max variant. 

The Touchscreen MacBook Pro 14-inch starts at $2,899, and the 16-inch version starts at $3,399. 

Consumers can place a preorder for the new touchscreen MacBook Pro from October 30, and the device will be available starting November 6.

The new Touchscreen MacBook marks two marquee product launches for new CEO John Ternus, who also introduced the company’s first foldable, the iPhone Duo, in September. Various Apple executives, including Steve Jobs and Tim Cook, have scoffed at the idea of a touchscreen Mac in the past. Jobs famously called the idea “ergonomically terrible” at one point. However, rumors of the company working on such a variant started circulating nearly three years before today’s introduction.

The launch follows yesterday’s unveiling of a new standard MacBook Pro with the M6 chip in 14-inch size starting from $1,999.

title: Chrome’s AI-powered Autofill can now dig through your Gmail to fill out forms
snippet: The autofill update lets Chrome pull flight confirmations, tracking info, order details, and other information from your inbox, with your permission.
fullText:
In Brief

Posted:

10:00 AM PDT · October 28, 2026

Image Credits:Google

		

							

											
									

					

	

Google’s Chrome browser is getting an update that will improve its autofill capabilities using AI. On Wednesday, the company said that Chrome will get an advanced version of autofill that will help users fill out online forms with suggestions pulled from their Gmail.

That means Chrome could suggest things you might need to know, like a flight confirmation number, membership ID, tracking information, order number, address, phone number, or credit card number by referencing your email.

The update is an expansion of Google’s Personal Intelligence, which already allows users to connect their Google Apps to its AI assistant, Gemini, to retrieve certain details and then use them to answer complex questions.

Though seemingly minor, the update could make Chrome easier to use, which could give users another reason to continue to use Google’s browser and stay in its AI ecosystem. It’s reminiscent of one of Apple’s most appreciated features: the ability to automatically detect verification codes sent via text and display them above the keyboard, allowing users to enter them with a single tap.

As with other Personalized Intelligence features, users can decide whether or not to enable enhanced autofill from their Chrome settings. Sensitive data is encrypted, Google notes.

The feature is rolling out to U.S. users on the desktop, and in the iOS and Android apps for Gemini in Chrome.

title: Apple addressed at least 329 unique security vulnerabilities across today’s system updates
snippet: Apple has updated its security releases page with details of the vulnerabilities addressed in today’s updates to iOS, iPadOS, macOS, watchOS, tvOS, visionOS, and Safari. Here are the details. more…
fullText:
Apple has updated its security releases page with details of the vulnerabilities addressed in today’s updates to iOS, iPadOS, macOS, watchOS, tvOS, visionOS, and Safari. Here are the details.

Apple details security releases from today’s updates

Whenever Apple releases software updates, the company also usually updates its security releases page with details of the vulnerabilities addressed.

Today, the company updated the page with the security content for the following system updates:

iPhone 11 and later, iPad Pro 12.9-inch 3rd generation and later, iPad Pro 11-inch 1st generation and later, iPad Air 3rd generation and later, iPad 8th generation and later, and iPad mini 5th generation and later

visionOS 27.2

Safari 27.2

This update has no published CVE entries.

Apple TV HD and Apple TV 4K 1st generation

In total, Apple addressed 329 unique security vulnerabilities across today’s software releases. Many of these vulnerabilities affect multiple operating systems, resulting in a whopping combined total of 1,265 CVE listings.

These numbers may still increase, as Apple regularly adds new entries and updates existing ones in its security advisories after their initial publication.

Among the most notable security fixes are a CoreMedia issue that could let a malicious app access the camera on an iPhone, iPad, Mac, or Apple Vision Pro without permission (CVE-2026-86990), and an Apple Intelligence vulnerability that could let a remote attacker access sensitive user data on supported iPhones and iPads (CVE-2026-86987).

Apple also addressed a Siri vulnerability in macOS Tahoe that could let an app access sensitive user data (CVE-2026-43736), along with multiple WebKit flaws that could allow maliciously crafted web content to execute arbitrary code.

Specifically, when it comes to WebKit, Apple has been on a security-patching spree in recent months, partly driven by the growing use of AI tools to uncover vulnerabilities. (In today’s updates alone, Apple credited AI tools and research teams for several vulnerabilities across its software.)

Earlier this year, the company also released multiple updates to fix flaws exploited by Coruna and DarkSword on older devices. Both exploit kits used WebKit vulnerabilities as part of attack chains that compromised iPhones running older versions of iOS.

And speaking of older versions of iOS, today’s updates also bring a previously released CoreGraphics fix to devices still running iOS 18 and iPadOS 18. The vulnerability could allow a maliciously crafted file to trigger arbitrary code execution (CVE-2026-86950).

Apple first addressed the issue in updates released last month, warning that it may have been exploited in an extremely sophisticated attack against specific targeted individuals running versions of iOS before iOS 27.

title: Microsoft just shared Azure’s actual revenue in dollars: $33.2 billion
snippet: Microsoft has never disclosed Azure's quarterly revenue in dollars. But for the first time, we can see just how close it is getting to besting the biggest competitor in the market, AWS.
fullText:
Microsoft has never disclosed Azure’s quarterly revenue in dollars. It has typically only shared a growth percentage or described revenue dollar milestones in vague ways. But on Wednesday, when it posted another record-breaking quarter, it reported that Azure brought in a healthy $33.2 billion in revenue for the July-September quarter, up 48% from a year earlier.

The disclosure lets investors line up Azure’s performance more directly against Amazon Web Services and Google Cloud, whose parent companies already report cloud revenue in dollars every quarter. 

Alphabet, which also reported earnings on Wednesday, said Google Cloud brought in $30.7 billion in the same quarter, putting Azure slightly ahead. But Google Cloud, which also includes Google’s Workspace subscriptions, roughly doubled its revenue from a year earlier, growing about twice as fast as Azure, according to TechCrunch’s calculations.

Azure, where businesses rent computing power to run applications, SaaS, and to build and run AI models, is now Microsoft’s largest and fastest-growing product line by the company’s own figures. It accounted for roughly 36% of Microsoft’s $92.3 billion in quarterly revenue.

Azure’s revenue was also about $850 million more than the $32.3 billion analysts expected. Azure’s 48% growth rate also topped the 44% to 45% that Microsoft CFO Amy Hood forecast on the company’s July earnings call.

Azure sits inside Agents and Infra, one of two new business segments Microsoft introduced this quarter. Microsoft previously reported three segments, Productivity and Business Processes, Intelligent Cloud, and More Personal Computing. The new Agents and Infra segment, which groups Azure with Microsoft 365’s cloud business, brought in $76.8 billion, up 25% from a year earlier.

Amazon reports its earnings on Thursday. Analysts also expect its cloud, Amazon Web Services, to grow. It’s been the largest cloud since the beginning of time and no one expects Microsoft to best it right now. But with all of them reporting actual dollars, the race is on.

title: Fox One Will Track 2026 Midterm Election Results With New App Experience
snippet: Fox’s streaming service adds a new layer of coverage to the 2026 midterm elections.
fullText:
The 2026 midterm elections are less than a week away, and Fox has unveiled a new interactive experience for Fox One app subscribers on Election Day, Tuesday, Nov. 3, to keep up with the news and results as they come in across the country.

With hundreds of House, Senate, gubernatorial and local races happening all at once, it can be tough to follow along with every update. According to a statement, Fox One has launched an interface to keep track of everything, “where a race in one state reframes the math in another and where what matters most to viewers may be a ballot measure in their own county.”

The Fox One election experience will add context to Fox’s broadcast coverage.Fox One

The features that’ll appear as part of this rollout include a command center on the Fox One home screen, with widgets that update in real time on things like voter polls, contest results and Fox News “Election Insights” on key races; a curated election hub that’ll include all of Fox’s election coverage; and a new Elections Mode version of Ask Fox, the app’s AI-powered chatbot, where viewers can ask election-based questions and receive answers in real time.

			

More from CNET

“The results don’t arrive in order, and no two viewers are following the same set of races,” said Amit Dudakia, senior vice president and head of product at Fox Direct to Consumer. “With Fox One, we’re keeping coverage from Fox News and Fox Stations at the center and building the context around it, so viewers aren’t toggling between a stream and a second screen to understand what just happened.”

Fox One’s complete channel portfolio includes Fox News Channel, Fox Nation, Fox Sports, B1G, FS1, FS2, the Fox Network and local Fox stations. It is available at no additional cost for cable and satellite TV customers and is priced at $20 a month for a stand-alone subscription to the app. The new in-app election experience will launch on Election Day.

title: You Can Spend Nearly $15K on Apple’s New Touchscreen MacBook Pro. Why?
snippet: Maxing out the new touchscreen MacBook Pro with a M5 Max chip and 16TB of storage will cost more than buying 10 basic MacBook Air laptops.
fullText:
The new MacBook Pro with PROLED XDR Display, announced on Wednesday and available on Nov. 6, brings touchscreen control to Apple’s most premium laptop. Pricing starts at $2,899 for the entry-level M5 Pro with the smaller 14-inch display, or $3,399 for the 16-inch model, before any applicable education discounts.

If you go ham on Apple’s preorder configurator and max out the processor, memory and storage, the price balloons to an eye-watering $14,549. That’s wild, especially in today’s economy. Will anyone actually spend that?

Fully loading the M5 MacBook Pro

Let’s see what it means to reach that top-tier configuration of the new touchscreen laptop, starting with the larger, more expensive 16-inch PROLED XDR model at $3,399. Color doesn’t affect price, so take your pick of silver or space black.

			

More from CNET

The first upgrade you’ll pay for is Nano-texture glass, an antireflective glass finish physically etched at the nanometer scale to diffuse ambient light and eliminate glare, for an additional $150. 

Then, stepping up from the M5 Pro’s 20-core GPU to the M5 Max’s 35-core GPU brings the total to $4,949. Bumping to the even more potent 40-core GPU adds another $300, while unlocking horsepower for complex tasks like gaming, video editing and AI-driven operations such as machine learning and coding. (In our testing, CNET found that the Max 40-core is the best fit for pro creatives who work with 8K or raw video, data scientists and intensive users of generative AI imaging and video.) 

Next comes memory and storage, which is where things get really expensive. Our starting M5 Max configuration comes standard with 48GB of unified memory and 2TB of storage, but we can pump those numbers considerably. Upgrading to 128GB of memory adds $2,000. Going for 16TB of storage adds $7,000, the most expensive upgrade on the list, roughly doubling the price of the machine. 

Pricey high-capacity memory and storage were par for the course long before the RAMpocalypse, but the current AI-fueled spike in RAM and solid-state storage prices has made things worse.

“It’s so expensive because 16TB drives cost a fortune, as does 128GB, and professionals have been paying those workstation prices for years,” Lori Grunin, CNET senior editor for computers and gaming hardware, told me.

Maxing the RAM boosts bandwidth and performance, allowing the Mac to more easily work with the massive files used in high-resolution video, complex 3D models, large datasets and complex mathematical equations. The extra terabytes of storage mean more and larger files can be saved to the device, since neither the MacBook’s memory nor storage can be upgraded after purchase. 

All in, our fully loaded MacBook Pro M5 Max with 16-inch PROLED XDR Display comes to $14,549. 

Grunin said she’d want more for the money. “For that price, I’d expect the M5 Ultra chip,” she said. “But I don’t think they can put the Ultra in a laptop yet.”

The top-spec MacBooks are aimed at companies that can absorb the high costs of high-capacity storage and memory.Apple

These upgrades aren’t for everyday people

So who buys a laptop that costs more than a used car? Is this just a flex for the super-rich?

“It’s for people who don’t have to pay for it,” said CNET Managing Editor Joshua Goldman.

Configured-to-order, powerful mobile workstations like these are most commonly bought through enterprise procurement by companies, startups and institutions — so the employer is paying, not the individual. Think engineering and architecture firms, Hollywood VFX and post-production houses or AI, machine learning and data science teams. They have big budgets, can put the extra digital horsepower to use and can easily absorb the exorbitant price.

For context, Grunin pointed me to a Dell Precision workstation that I was able to trick out to over $18,000. Five-figure enterprise-scale machines from HP or Lenovo are also not out of the question.

Yes, there will be well-heeled individuals buying at this level, but they’re a relatively small slice of the pie. More likely, the majority of the new touch-enabled MacBook Pros sold will be at still-expensive but easier-to-fathom prices.

title: Xreal Aura is a new wired headset powered by Android XR
snippet: Xreal Aura will start at $1,279 and will have multiple XR specific apps at launch.
fullText:
At the Android Dev Summit on Wednesday, Google’s smart glasses partner Xreal launched its new Xreal Aura wired smart glasses, powered by the Android XR and Qualcomm’s Snapdragon Reality Elite platforms. The companies had teased the glasses earlier in the year at Google’s I/O developer conference.

As Meta expands its push into smart glasses, competitors like Apple and Google are keen to release their own devices. Much like it did with Android smartphones, Google is relying on an assortment of partners, including Samsung and Xreal, to bring devices powered by its Android XR platform to consumers.

The new Xreal Aura smart glasses are tethered to a smartphone-like device for processing power, rather than handling all the computing themselves. The glasses then display the content in the wearer’s field of view. 

The device’s design, meanwhile, is closer to Meta’s smart glasses than Apple’s Vision Pro, which is a larger headset.

Xreal Aura uses Sony’s Micro-OLED display with 1200p resolution at 120 Hz and a 95-degree field of view — screen specs that put the glasses above the Ray-Ban Meta Display on paper. However, Xreal’s smart glasses are heavier at 95 grams compared to Meta’s 69 grams, and you have to carry the puck.

At launch, the Aura supports many popular Google Play apps and games along with specific XR experiences, including the NBA App for Android XR; Nevatars; Fallout: Factions; Project Hail Mary: Journey Among the Stars; the NASCAR XR App; and the San Francisco Ballet Company’s “The Nutcracker.”

Users can opt to plug a computer or handheld gaming console directly into the Xreal Aura via USB-C to make it an augmented display. The device can also allow for various entertainment and productivity use cases by spinning up a multimonitor setup or a big virtual screen.

For audio, the Xreal Aura uses Bose’s tech to power its sound while watching videos or listening to music.

Given that the new smart glasses are powered by Android XR, Gemini is available to users as a Q&A assistant and can help them understand on-screen context.

The Xreal Aura is available to order starting today in the United States, Canada, Japan, and

South Korea. The 12GB + 256GB version costs $1,279 with a limited launch price of $1,099 through December, and the 16GB + 512GB version is priced at $1,499 with a launch price of $1,299 through December. The company said it will start shipping by mid-November.

In May, Xreal CEO Chi Xu told TechCrunch that building a smart glass business is hard and everyone is losing money. He also said that the Aura glasses will have a wide range of use cases, and the industry has reached an inflection point of having the right hardware, software, and design smart glasses to reach scale.

“You need all the key pieces ready — you need the hardware ready, the operating system needs to be ready, and then you need a great user interface,” Xu said at that time.

When you purchase through links in our articles, we may earn a small commission. This doesn’t affect our editorial independence.

		

Ivan covers global consumer tech developments at TechCrunch. He is based out of India and has previously worked at publications including Huffington Post and The Next Web.

title: The MacBook Pro OLED Isn’t the Touchscreen Mac I Was Looking For
snippet: Commentary: Apple finally put touch on a MacBook Pro, but at a price and form that confuses me.
fullText:
I’ve been on a mission for a decade and a half to see that Apple fuses its iPad and Mac lines into something that would be the best of both worlds. I’ve been told that iPads and Macs would never merge, and that touch would never come to Macs. Well, Macs have touchscreens now, or at least one of them; the awkwardly named “MacBook Pro with PROLED XDR Display” is the very first, arriving Nov. 6.

I’ve been reviewing iPads for years, and I also specialize in reviewing new forms of computing, such as VR/AR headsets and AI-enabled wearables. My hope is that these devices would evolve into true computers that could replace my laptop.

iPads have come awfully close, but the OS and app compatibility still creates a slight divide, meaning certain pro apps and browser tools don’t work the same way. But iPads have the form, the touchscreens, the transforming designs, the modular accessories and support for the wonderful Pencil. I argued earlier this year that the MacBook Neo, with a similar-to-iPad price and an iPhone/iPad-level chipset, showed how close Macs and iPads are getting. I can see a connecting thread, and it excites me.

			

More from CNET

I say all this because the new MacBook Pros, which I haven’t tried myself, add touchscreens but barely do anything at all to the laptop’s design itself. Instead of folding back or even flat, the screen hinge merely tilts to standard laptop angles and hangs in place while you touch the upright surface. 

While Apple is pitching the new MacBook touch features as a great way to interact with MacOS, it doesn’t look, at first glance, that MacOS has evolved to accommodate touch input in truly transformative ways…or in workflows that already perform wonderfully on iPhones and iPads.

Clearly, to me at least, Apple is on a transformation path. The iPhone Duo fuses parts of iPhone and iPad and aims to augment the phone experience with that of a tablet. Similar opportunities lie ahead for Macs and iPads: sure, you may not want MacOS as it exists now on an iPad, but I’d definitely want a touch-evolved MacOS fusion to live on an iPad that could transform into every Mac/iPad need I desire. Would that be worth a higher price? Sure.

The touchscreen MacBook Pro we’re getting at the end of 2026 isn’t that computer. It’s not something most people can afford, anyway, at $2,899 and up. But when I think of touch on a Mac, kids and families using it come to mind. Or, drawing with the Apple Pencil, which you can’t do on this touchscreen MacBook. Or having it be a useful way to access apps that currently live on iPads and iPhones and could, in a pinch, run on the Mac. For iMacs, it could be fun. For convertible MacBooks, it could redefine what a Mac is relative to an iPad.

All I can think of is, what if this Mac could fold back and work with Apple Pencil?Tara Brown/CNET

This feels like a foot in the door for Apple, and an odd one at that. The name “MacBook Pro with PROLED XDR Display” doesn’t even reference touch at all, and Apple’s marketing seems to underplay the touch-on-Mac debut. The real star of the show is the new OLED display, which truly is a pro feature for a MacBook. The touch extras feel like they’re added in as a bonus.

Now, it all could end up feeling better and more useful than I’m thinking right now. And yes, I’ve often reached up to my MacBook Air to touch the screen, especially after working on an iPad for a while. Almost all the other computers in 2026 have touchscreens, anyway, even in laptop form.

But with all the promises iPads already deliver on for touch, Macs deserve better. And I’m hoping 2027 is when Apple really gets into a transformative discussion about how touch-enabled Macs, and all existing and future iPads, can evolve next. The future Apple computer I’m envisioning doesn’t exist yet, but it’s getting close. And I’m optimistically thinking Apple can address it soon, but as always, you never know.

		

				

					

						

													

					

					

						

Scott Stein
						

						

							Editor at Large						
					

											

								

											I started with CNET reviewing laptops in 2009. Now I explore wearable tech, VR/AR, tablets, gaming and future/emerging trends in our changing world. Other obsessions include magic, immersive theater, puzzles, board games, cooking, improv and the New York Jets. My background includes an MFA in theater which I apply to thinking about immersive experiences of the future.

title: DoorDash to acquire Instacart for $17B
snippet: The acquisition would bring two major players in on-demand delivery under one roof, combining DoorDash’s dominance in restaurant takeout with Instacart’s reach in grocery delivery.
fullText:
DoorDash announced on Thursday that it has agreed to acquire rival Instacart for $17 billion. The acquisition would bring two major players in on-demand delivery under one roof, combining DoorDash’s dominance in restaurant takeout with Instacart’s reach in grocery delivery. 

DoorDash will buy Instacart for a total value of $65 for each Instacart share, the company said. The deal has been approved by the boards of both companies.

“Over the last 14 years, Instacart has transformed online grocery by helping retailers of all sizes compete and grow, and joining forces with DoorDash allows us to do even more,” said Instacart CEO Chris Rogers in a press release. 

“When our purpose-built grocery technology and trusted retailer and brand relationships are combined with DoorDash’s global consumer reach and logistics capabilities, we can create new opportunities for our retail and brand partners, offer an even better experience for customers and shoppers, and deliver compelling value for our shareholders.”

DoorDash plans to keep Instacart’s brand, enterprise technology products, and app. The company also notes that the two brands will continue to operate as separate and independent companies until the transaction closes.

DoorDash says the deal could help more grocers build out their own online ordering platforms and advertising businesses using Instacart’s technology, while grocers could also use DoorDash’s fulfillment services to handle more online orders and offer lower-cost delivery.

“Grocery is one of the hardest things to get right online,” DoorDash CEO Tony Xu said in the press release. 

“Someone has to pick a ripe avocado, find a substitute you’d choose yourself, and get the ice cream to you before it melts. Instacart has spent years learning to do that well for grocers, while DoorDash has built a delivery network and technology that local stores rely on every day. Together, we could give stores of every size more of those tools and unlock the potential of grocery delivery. It’s still early innings, but we know that when more people shop local, more dollars stay local,” said Xu.

Instacart currently has a market cap of more than $13 billion, and its stock price is up 25% for the year to date. The company likely viewed this as an opportune time to sell at a desirable price, ahead of intensifying competition in the grocery delivery market.

Bloomberg previously reported that Instacart was in talks with Uber, but that the company had walked away from discussions. 

The deal is expected to close toward the end of 2027 or in the first half of 2028.

Aisha is a consumer news reporter at TechCrunch. Prior to joining the publication in 2021, she was a telecom reporter at MobileSyrup. Aisha holds an honours bachelor’s degree from University of Toronto and a master’s degree in journalism from Western University.

fullText:
DoorDash has announced that it’s buying Instacart in a deal valued at approximately $17 billion. The acquisition will give DoorDash a bigger presence in online grocery delivery thanks to Instacart’s established grocery marketplace and retailer partnerships, with Instacart CEO Chris Rogers saying the deal will make “online grocery more seamless and affordable” for millions of households.

DoorDash says the acquisition will give Instacart users acces to more than 50,000 additional stores, and allow DashPass and Instacart Plus members to “pay one membership fee instead of two.” The deal is expected to close “in the end of 2027 or the first half of 2028,” subject to regulatory approvals and other closing conditions. When finalized, DoorDash says it will preserve Instacart’s brand, enterprise technology products, and app, so the services will remain separate instead of being merged into a single platform.

In its post-close commitments, DoorDash said local grocers won’t be limited by platform exclusivity, and will be free to work with either delivery service. Instacart shoppers will also retain flexibility around their working hours and which orders to accept, and will be able to choose whether to take on DoorDash orders or just stick with shopping for Instacart.

DoorDash, which started as a restaurant courier service, already has its own grocery delivery business, but that faces ongoing competition from Instacart, Uber, Walmart, and Amazon. DoorDash is also incentivized to diversify further because its rivals have been stepping into the food delivery territory it’s best known for, with Uber acquiring Postmates and Delivery Hero.

Here’s what DoorDash said regarding increasing competition:

“Most grocery shopping still happens in stores, but more people are buying groceries and everyday goods online. They expect fast, affordable delivery and an easy way to order. The biggest online retailers and grocers are racing ahead, building their own delivery fleets, warehouses, membership programs, and AI shopping assistants. A grocer or retailer running on thin margins cannot build all of that alone, and with AI, the playing field risks being tilted even further away from local commerce.”

Rumors around the deal started circulating last week after The Information reported that Instacart was in talks with rival platforms Uber and DoorDash regarding a potential sale. By Monday, The Wall Street Journal reported that DoorDash was in “advanced talks” with Instacart, and that a deal could be reached “as soon as this week.” That proved to be accurate, though finalization will take much longer — giving stockholders and regulators time to voice their feelings about the acquisition.

“Grocery is one of the hardest things to get right online,” DoorDash CEO Tony Xu said in the announcement. “Instacart has spent years learning to do that well for grocers, while DoorDash has built a delivery network and technology that local stores rely on every day. Together, we could give stores of every size more of those tools and unlock the potential of grocery delivery.”

title: Apple knows the iPad mini market, but internet unimpressed by 60Hz
snippet: Apple yesterday officially launched what it describes as “the biggest update ever” to the iPad mini, featuring an OLED screen and a thinner, lighter design. However, while there are a significant number of upgrades, internet commentators were very focused on the one thing Apple didn’t upgrade: that 60Hz display … more…
fullText:
Apple yesterday officially launched what it describes as “the biggest update ever” to the iPad mini, featuring an OLED screen and a thinner, lighter design.

However, while there are a significant number of upgrades, internet commentators were very focused on the one thing Apple didn’t upgrade: that 60Hz display … 

Apple highlighted the new features.

A stunning OLED display in an even thinner and lighter design, a huge leap in performance with A20 Pro, and water and dust resistance. The larger 8.5-inch OLED display, also available with a nano-texture option, delivers higher contrast and more than 2x higher peak brightness than the previous-generation iPad mini for a brilliant and immersive viewing experience. A20 Pro supercharges AI with Neural Accelerators in each GPU core and Dual 16-core Neural Engine. iPad mini now has a 12MP Center Stage front camera on the landscape edge that’s perfect for video calls, an innovative Acoustic Display for an even better audio experience, faster wireless and cellular connectivity, and fast-charge support.

Commenters, however, were quick to point to the fact that the refresh rate wasn’t mentioned, with the obvious conclusion that it remains 60Hz instead of being updated to a ProMotion variable refresh rate of 1 to 120Hz.

“700 bucks and no 120hz display?”

“I was someone interested in adding a mini but at 60hz, 128gb, no Face ID I can’t justify the already inflated price tag.”

“60Hz right? in 2026 right? Hell no.”

“60Hz? Next…”

“60Hz in 2026. Apple should be ashamed.”

	

I could include many more quotes, but you get the idea. It’s certainly a surprising omission in a 2026 device, especially when our sister site 9to5Google noted that the closest Android competitor has a 185Hz refresh rate.

The biggest point in Redmagic’s favor is in that display, too. Where Apple is still refusing to give the iPad Mini a 120Hz refresh rate with this latest model – utterly insane in the year two thousand and twenty-six, if I do say so myself – Astra 2 has a 185Hz refresh rate. I’ve not found that inherently better than a standard 120Hz panel, but it’s way better than the 60Hz panel Apple’s latest will still be using.

Now I fully acknowledge that Apple knows the iPad mini market better than any of us do. I’m also aware that it has historically been primarily a business device, used for applications ranging from restaurant waitstaff relaying orders to the kitchen through mobile payment terminals to warehouse inventory systems. None of these types of applications would remotely benefit from a display with a faster refresh rate.

Additionally, when it comes to consumers, I’m sure it’s true that not everyone appreciates the benefits of 120Hz. Some of those in our comments claimed they couldn’t tell the difference, while others said it was only really relevant to gaming. Adding that category of individual purchasers to the majority business market, and Apple has undoubtedly correctly concluded that the majority of its customers simply don’t care about this feature. 

However … Those who do care about it, care about it rather a lot. I don’t know what the unit cost difference would be, but since 120Hz is now standard on a great many cheaper devices, I can’t imagine it’s a substantial one. I can’t help feeling that this is a case where Apple simply should have done the right thing, even if only a minority of buyers would appreciate it.

title: Amazon announced five new Alexa devices, including 16-inch Echo Show
snippet: Apple recently launched new HomePod mini speakers and its HomeView smart display, and today it’s Amazon’s turn with five new Alexa devices. This includes a new Echo speaker with visual intelligence and an Echo Show with a larger 16-inch display and a nanomatte option … more…
fullText:
Apple recently launched new HomePod mini speakers and its HomeView smart display, and today it’s Amazon’s turn with five new Alexa devices.

This includes a new Echo speaker with visual intelligence and an Echo Show with a larger 16-inch display and a nanomatte option …

Echo Dot

The latest smart device lineup kicks off with a next-generation Echo Dot speaker, which includes a home hub, on-device AI capabilities, and a built-in Wi-Fi extender.

For the first time, it includes a built-in smart home hub, so Alexa connects to thousands of compatible devices such as lights, locks, and thermostats right out of the box—plus a built-in eero Wi-Fi extender adds up to 1,000 square feet of coverage to your existing network. At its core is Amazon’s custom AZ3 silicon, with a new AI Accelerator for on-device AI that sharpens conversational detection and filters out background noise. Music, audiobooks, and podcasts sound great on the new Echo Dot, with crisp vocals and 50% more bass than its predecessor.

The Dot is available today for $99.99, with special Kids editions for $109.99 that include a one-year subscription to Amazon Kids+.

Echo Studio with Home Camera

The Echo Studio is a better speaker that now includes HomePod-like room mapping and a camera that allows a live view of your home as well as Alexa-powered visual intelligence features.

Echo Studio with Home Camera takes Amazon’s best-sounding speaker and gives it a richer understanding of the room around it, making Alexa even more useful. The same powerful audio architecture is still at its core—a high-excursion woofer and Dolby Atmos filling the room with immersive spatial sound, now continuously tuned to your space with Advanced Room Adaptation. What’s new is context: with more awareness of its surroundings, Alexa can help in real time—explaining the rules on a board game box you hold up, recognizing a box of cereal to help you reorder it, or letting you check in on the room from the Alexa app while you’re away.

The original Echo Studio without the camera is $219.99, while the new model is available today at $249.99.

Echo Time smart bedside clock

The new Echo Time has a display that gradually brightens to mimic a sunrise as your alarm time approaches, and a sleep sensor provides the option of waking you when you’re in a lighter sleep phase.

Echo Time is purpose-built for the bedside—with a customizable display and camera-free design to make waking up and winding down effortless. Make it yours with hundreds of clock faces to choose from—including everything from analog and modern to playful designs and even your favorite sports teams. Its new sleep sensing technology, powered by Omnisense, can sense when you’re in lighter sleep and wakes you within 10 to 60 minutes of your scheduled alarm, no wearable device required. As your alarm approaches, the display gradually brightens to mimic a natural sunrise and the tone builds gently to help ease you awake.

The standard model is available today for $199.99, with a kids version again at $10 more with a year of Kids+ included.

Alexa Photo Frame

	

A new photo frame syncs to Amazon Photos to show the latest photos as you take them, with the ability to ask Alexa to find the photos you want to display.

Most of the photos we love never leave our phones. The Alexa Photo Frame changes that—pairing the timeless elegance of a traditional frame with the intelligence of Alexa, so your best memories are always on display. It’s the first photo frame with Alexa built in, and it works effortlessly: connect it to Amazon Photos and your pictures sync automatically, with new ones appearing as they’re taken. Alexa intelligently surfaces the shots worth seeing—the ones where you’re smiling, in the right season—and skips the screenshots and clutter. Just ask to see photos of a favorite person, pet, or trip, or swipe through right on the 10-inch anti-glare touchscreen, where every picture looks crisp and vibrant from any angle.

The Alexa Photo Frame is available today for $199.99 in black or $229 in real birch or walnut.

Echo Show 16

Finally, the tablet-like Echo Show 15 has been upgraded to offer 10% more viewing area on a 16-inch screen in a thinner device with a nanomatte anti-reflective option. Like Apple’s HomeView, there are options for placing on a countertop via an iMac-like stand or mounting on a wall.

The all-new Echo Show 16 is our most advanced display yet, with 20% more power for interactions that feel fast. The 16-inch high-definition screen is nearly 40% thinner with 10% more viewing area, and a new Nanomatte option cuts glare by more than 90% while keeping detail and color razor-sharp. Screen Styles transform it into whatever your home needs most—a family organizer with color-coded calendars, chores, and meal plans; a digital photo frame; or a smart home dashboard with the new Alexa Home Map, showing every light, lock, thermostat, and camera right where it lives in your home. Plus, it has the full Fire TV experience, built in. Echo Show 16 has our best-ever camera on an Echo Show, featuring the widest field of view, auto-framing that keeps everyone in view, and—for the first time—night vision, so you can check in with Live View day or night.

The Echo Show 16 is available for pre-order today at $499.99 or $569.99 with the nanomatte screen. Availability hasn’t yet been confirmed, with the company simply saying that it will begin shipping “later this year.”

title: Android 17-based Redmagic OS 12 gets closer to a global release
snippet: The global rollout schedule is still a bit of a mystery, but we at least know which Redmagic devices are getting the Redmagic OS 12 Android 17 upgrade. more…
fullText:
The global rollout schedule is still a bit of a mystery, but we at least know which Redmagic devices are getting the Redmagic OS 12 Android 17 upgrade.

Redmagic is updating 8 of its latest devices to Android 17 in China, which began with the launch of the Redmagic 12 Pro+. Redmagic calls its Android 17 skin “Redmagic OS 12,” and the update includes a slew of visual changes, more AI integration, simplified connectivity and file transfer to iPhones, and a bunch of gaming and performance upgrades. Here’s the timeline:

December 2026: Redmagic 11 Pro and Redmagic 11S Pro series

January 2027: Redmagic Gaming Tablet 5 Pro

March 2027: Redmagic 10 Pro series, Redmagic 10S Pro series, Redmagic 11 Air, and Redmagic eSports Tablet 3 Pro

April 2027: Redmagic 10 Air

While these are technically the Chinese upgrade dates, we expect Redmagic to follow with global availability shortly afterward. Redmagic 12 Pro gets a global release date on November 3, 2026, so a global version of Redmagic OS 12 is already finished and just needs to be ported to these other devices.

As is the case with many Android 17 updates, this one focuses on a visual redesign that includes more Liquid Glass-inspired design, including a giant lockscreen clock and new lockscreen customizations. A Dynamic Island-like feature called AI Magic Island adorns the status bar and expands for actionable notifications like music playback, ride-hailing, and more, presumably using Android 17’s Live Updates feature.

	

The MORA AI companion is a new VTuber-like AI assistant that’s now built into the phone, and Redmagic is also including new “AI Magic Assistant” automated task executions to go along with it. A refreshed Game Space app is included in the OS update, as well as an Esports Training Arena app with built-in shooting and reaction mini-games, plus the X-Gravity Platform 3.0 update and upgraded live streaming capabilities.

Apple says: 

Apple today announced the new 14-inch MacBook Pro with M6, delivering even more performance, powerful on-device AI capabilities, and faster connectivity for college students, business users, creators, and more. M6 features an advanced 12-core CPU with the world’s fastest CPU core, so everything from productivity tasks to more demanding pro workflows feels incredibly fast and responsive.

In terms of performance, Apple says: 

The 12-core GPU is up to 30% faster than M5. 

The dual 16-core Neural Engine is up to 1.9x faster than M5. 

Up to 13x faster time to first token performance for LLM prompt processing compared to the 13-inch MacBook Pro with M1, and up to 1.3x faster than the 14-inch MacBook Pro with M5.

title: Some Pixel Watch users report a sudden decrease in battery life
snippet: A surge of online reports indicates that some users are experiencing a recent increase in battery drain on their Pixel Watch, by as much as 20% every few hours. more…
fullText:
A surge of online reports indicates that some users are experiencing a recent increase in battery drain on their Pixel Watch, by as much as 20% every few hours.

Sometimes new software introduces extra stress on device batteries. New processes can take a toll on phone or smartwatch energy at a higher cost than expected, and that might be what’s happening with some Pixel Watch users.

It’s nowhere near a definitive trend, but it’s intriguing to see several new posts on Reddit pop up with the same complaint – their Pixel Watch’s battery is draining faster than normal (via Android Authority). One post has 65 comments, with a healthy number sharing the same concern. One user wrote that their Pixel Watch 2 is getting 12 hours of use on a full charge, instead of the normal 48 hours with AOD off.

The other user claims their Pixel Watch 4 now lasts less than a day. Their normal usage reportedly gets them up to 2.5 days. That’s high for the Pixel Watch 4, but it’s not unheard of. Both of these users dropping by 12 or 24 hours from one charge isn’t nothing.

	
	

Sporadic comments echo the same situation, but many report they haven’t noticed a difference. Timing isn’t entirely consistent across comments, either. Some say they started seeing the issue a few days ago, while others say this happened to them a while back.

Still, it might indicate a recent software update is to blame. Google’s recent September 2026 update reaches the Pixel Watch 2 and newer. It adds “Gemini Personalization,” which Google says leverages past conversations and Google apps like Gmail or Calendar to offer personalized responses. It’s also possible that the battery is affected by the recent Google Health update with automatic activity tracking, but that wouldn’t explain why the Pixel Watch 2 is having an issue.

It’s unclear if that’s playing a factor, but Google has yet to officially acknowledge the issue for these users.

What about you? Is your Pixel Watch suddenly dying in the middle of the day? The comments section is all yours.

title: US government acting illegally over electronic surveillance of its own citizens, say senators
snippet: Two senators with notable expertise in intelligence matters say that the US government is acting illegally over electronic surveillance of its own citizens. They say the Foreign Intelligence Surveillance Court (FISC) has permitted intelligence agencies to continue warrantless interception of messages by US citizens despite failing to comply with the administration’s own privacy promise to allow public review of such rulings … more…
fullText:
Two senators with notable expertise in intelligence matters say that the US government is acting illegally over electronic surveillance of its own citizens.

They say the Foreign Intelligence Surveillance Court (FISC) has permitted intelligence agencies to continue warrantless interception of messages by US citizens despite failing to comply with the administration’s own privacy promise to allow public review of such rulings …

The Foreign Intelligence Surveillance Act (FISA) was supposed to allow interception of communications by agents of foreign powers on US soil. It also put in place safeguards intended to ensure proper oversight. Controversially, however, it has also been used to intercept the communications of American citizens without a warrant under a clause known as Section 702.

That latter power is supposed to be granted for 12 months at a time by FISC. Decisions to renew the authorization should be made public within 180 days. It was last renewed back in March, with a deadline for public review expiring on September 13th. 

As Wired reports, however, that has still not happened.

Seven months ago, the Foreign Intelligence Surveillance Court objected to search filters that let intelligence analysts pull Americans’ messages from intercepted data without the approvals, written justifications, or records the law requires. The court approved another year of surveillance anyway. The ruling has never been made public, and Senators Ron Wyden of Oregon and Adam Schiff of California say the administration’s own deadline for releasing it passed in September […]

“If this administration won’t follow this simple statutory directive,” the senators told Director of National Intelligence Jay Clayton and Attorney General Todd Blanche in a demand letter obtained exclusively by WIRED, “it is unclear why Congress or the American people should trust this administration to follow any of the other legal limits to Section 702.”

The report also says that additional oversight through things like internal auditing within the FBI has been abandoned, and it’s no longer possible to track how many times search filters have been used to restrict electronic surveillance to US citizens.

Wyden is the longest-serving member of the Senate Intelligence Committee, and Schiff formerly chaired the equivalent House committee.

title: Boston Dynamics Faces Employee Protest Over Robot Deal With ICE
snippet: Tech workers have become increasingly vocal when their employers’ business deals clash with their values.
fullText:
Two months after reports that the robotics company Boston Dynamics would supply US Immigration and Customs Enforcement with some of its four-legged products resembling metal dogs, the company says it has no plans to abandon the deal despite objections from hundreds of employees.

The controversy began in late August, with reports that ICE planned to spend up to $2 million on Spot robot devices made by Boston Dynamics. According to documents supporting the purchase, the robot dogs would be used to listen for movement inside buildings and do searches in places humans can’t reach.

In September, employees sent management a petition, although the company has said it can’t verify that all of the more than 300 signatures are from Boston Dynamics staff because it claims nearly half of them were signed anonymously.

			

More from CNET

The Boston radio station WBUR posted a copy of the employee petition, minus signatures, which was sent to what the petition called “top management” on Sept. 8. In the letter, employees say they have been proud of the work they’ve done at Boston Dynamics, but the deal presents them as working directly with ICE: “We cannot be proud of working at BD when that work is being used by a government agency that brutalizes civilians, including some of our own colleagues at Hyundai.” In September 2025, ICE raided a Hyundai facility in Georgia and detained hundreds of workers, many of them from South Korea. Hyundai owns Boston Dynamics.

The letter expresses concerns that, in addition to making employees uncomfortable, the deal will cause Boston Dynamics to lose employees and will make the company a less attractive employer as it tries to grow. “The risk for BD is simply too great to continue with this deal,” the letter states.

Boston Dynamics stands firm on its sale

The petition didn’t block the sale of the robots, which was approved in late September by the government and acquired through a company called Radeco, which installed software called Cerberus.

Boston Dynamics told CNET in an email that it addressed the petition in several ways, starting with a letter to the petitioners from the company’s interim CEO, Amanda McMaster, that made clear the company was going ahead with the sale.

“We consider this decision final, and it’s time to move forward… I ask you to respect and accept this decision, even if you do not agree with it,” she wrote in a message sent to petitioners a week after the petition was received. 

The company’s defense of the sale has been that its terms and conditions of sale for customers make it explicit that its products cannot be used to harm people. “Those T&Cs prohibit any attempts to weaponize our robot or use it for purposes of harm or intimidation,” McMaster wrote. 

Boston Dynamics said it gave employees additional information about the ICE deal (the company had an existing relationship with the Department of Homeland Security), hosted roundtables about ethics and explained its decision-making process. In the company’s mind, at least, employee sentiment has shifted with additional information, and the company has been putting out information about how the robot canines will be used and why it’s working with ICE. “Spot robots are tools that help keep people out of harm’s way. Regardless of any political implications or personal feelings about the organizations involved, if our robot can help keep people safe, we believe it should,” a spokesperson said in a background document about the controversy the company provided to CNET.

Can employee protests make a difference?

At the very least, the Boston Dynamics employee petition caused the company to explain in detail why it was providing its products to ICE and created conversation within the company about its mission and direction going forward, even if it didn’t alter the terms of the sale or cancel it entirely.

Employee protests have become common in the tech industry in recent years, especially as AI is increasingly used in military applications. Google employees recently resigned over a military contract, and a 2018 protest led the company to decline to renew a Department of Defense contract. That same year, Microsoft was called out by employees for work it was doing with ICE.

Jamie E. Wright, a California employment attorney and founder of Wright Law Firm, said employee protests like these are often a way for employees to exercise the power they have to effect change in their workplaces. “They can play a big role in these situations,” she said, but “it’s never guaranteed.”

“While Boston Dynamics may not back down from their decision, employees can show that there are people that care and want to help prevent this from happening in the future,” Wright said. “Employees may not get what they are asking for in these situations, but they can open the doors to allow for changes.”

While protesting against labor conditions may offer some protection from retaliation, calling out an employer’s business deals likely doesn’t, she said. “Some states allow greater protection for political practices or off-duty activities that are legal. Some do not protect at all,” Wright said.

Debra Guckenheimer, a sociologist who closely follows employee protests, said that when people petition for change at their workplace, “That is a sign that they are concerned about retaliation.”

“The job market is very rough right now, and employees who are immigrants, especially immigrants of color, are under enormous pressure at this time,” Guckenheimer said. “The petition represents a lot of bravery and risk.”

Working in a place that is acting in ways that go against an employee’s morals, she said, can be “crushing” and lead to mental and physical problems. Ultimately, Guckenheimer said, employees who protest their employer on moral grounds may have nothing to gain personally other than peace of mind.

“The people who signed the petition at Boston Dynamics are trying to act in not only their own interest to ensure their work does not violate their conscience. They are also trying to preserve the legacy of the company,” Guckenheimer said.

											Omar Gallaga has covered technology, digital culture and other topics for outlets including CNET, NPR, Wired, Texas Monthly, MSNBC, Consumer Reports, The Washington Post, the Los Angeles Times, The Atlantic and the Austin American-Statesman, where he was a longtime tech reporter, editor and podcaster. He lives in the Texas Hill Country.

fullText:
Mac users can now install macOS 27.2 Golden Gate, which expands the new Siri AI to five additional languages, making it available to millions more users. Here are the details.

Apple releases macOS 27.2 Golden Gate

During the “Surprise and Shine” event last September, Apple announced that Siri AI would soon expand support to five new languages, in addition to English, which was available at launch with macOS 27, iOS 27, and the rest of the 27 OS updates.

Today, with the release of macOS 27.2 and its counterparts, Siri AI is now available in French, Japanese, Korean, Portuguese, and Spanish.

The update also includes new gesture recognition tools in several built-in apps, which could be laying the groundwork for Apple’s upcoming touchscreen MacBook Pro, expected to be announced this Wednesday at the “Pro and Tell” event.

One minor change included in macOS 27.2 is the new Apple Music app icon, which replaces the familiar red-and-white design with a black-and-white version.

The change coincides with Apple’s unveiling of a new visual identity for Apple Music, featuring a colorful, sound-inspired logo. That said, it remains unclear whether that design will eventually make its way to the app icon, as Apple did with the recent Apple TV rebranding.

During the beta cycle for macOS 27.2, users reported a particularly frustrating bug that caused windows in Electron-based apps to randomly stop responding to dragging attempts. Restarting the Mac temporarily resolved the issue, but the problem could eventually return.

The bug appears to have been fixed in last week’s Release Candidate, which carried a different release build than today’s release, which is 26B123. Importantly, users with beta updates enabled may need to disable them to see the new build in Software Update.

Apple has yet to publish the release and security notes for macOS 27.2. Still, it’s a safe bet that the update also includes security fixes, so even if the new Siri AI languages aren’t relevant to you, installing it is still recommended.

title: New iPad mini has big limitation on all but one model
snippet: Today Apple unveiled its biggest update to the iPad mini yet, but if you’re looking to buy one, there’s a key limitation of the A20 Pro chip in every configuration but one. more…
fullText:
Today Apple unveiled its biggest update to the iPad mini yet, but if you’re looking to buy one, there’s a key limitation of the A20 Pro chip in every configuration but one.

A20 Pro chip in iPad mini drops CPU core and Dual 16-core Neural Engine in most configurations

Apple’s new iPad mini comes with significant upgrades like the larger display, thinner design, OLED display, and a powerful A20 Pro chip.

But if you’re interested in buying the iPad mini, not all models are created equal.

In fact, every configuration except the highest 512GB model includes a less powerful, binned A20 Pro chip.

According to Apple’s tech specs page, here’s the breakdown of the A20 Pro across different storage configurations.

Models with 128GB or 256GB storage:

5-core CPU with 2 super cores and 3 efficiency cores

7-core GPU

Neural Accelerators

Hardware-accelerated ray tracing

16-core Neural Engine

Models with 512GB storage:

6-core CPU with 2 super cores and 4 efficiency cores

7-core GPU

Neural Accelerators

Hardware-accelerated ray tracing

Dual 16-core Neural Engine

It’s not unusual for Apple to use binned chips at times in its products. But in most cases, the only drawback of those chips is having one less CPU or GPU core.

With iPad mini, you not only lose a CPU core, you also don’t get the Dual 16-core Neural Engine.

That feature is exclusive to high-end 512GB models. So both the 128GB and 256GB models—the majority of configurations—have only a 16-core Neural Engine.

	

It’s a significant limitation, and especially unfortunate since it applies to most models that Apple will sell.

The iPad mini has a higher than ever starting price of $699, and if you want the model with a full-featured A20 Pro chip, it will set you back $999 (or more, depending on cellular and nano-texture choices).

title: Reddit Is Adding ‘For You’ and ‘Following’ Feeds
snippet: The new feeds, similar to those used on TikTok, are rolling out worldwide.
fullText:
Reddit is giving users new ways to sift through its billions of posts. The move follows recent platform changes that eliminated RSS feeds and limited access to the site’s classic desktop layout, Old Reddit.

In a blog post published on Wednesday, Reddit says it will introduce For You and Following tabs, similar to those used on TikTok. The new tabs will roll out to Reddit users worldwide over the next few weeks.

The two feeds will work differently. For You is a discovery feed that recommends posts from subreddits you follow, but adds posts the algorithm believes will relate to your interests. The Following tab is made up strictly of posts from subreddits you’ve already joined. Switching between them might give you a choice between a broader view of what’s on Reddit and one made up only of what you’ve curated for yourself as your interests.

			

More from CNET

The two new feeds, the company said, are part of its experiments to help people “more intentionally explore Reddit.”

User pushback against Reddit’s previous platform changes highlights a growing frustration with the site’s design evolution. These updates target RSS feeds, third-party API access, and Old Reddit availability, features long favored by users seeking alternatives to the default interface.

To keep browsing post archives, external apps must now transition to Reddit’s official developer platform or risk losing access entirely. Reddit reports that it is currently helping migrate roughly 14,000 apps to the new framework.

According to the company, the stricter policies are a necessary response to the rise of AI-driven bot traffic, which has surged dramatically and strained server infrastructure.

Apple Watch Series 12 and Apple Watch Ultra 4 are here, and later this year they’ll get even more powerful with two new features: Siri Recap and Live Rewind. Here are the details.

Siri AI is a major tentpole of watchOS 27, and later this year there’s a powerful Siri addition coming to Apple Watch Series 12 and Ultra 4. It’s called Siri Recap.

Siri Recap ambiently takes notes on your conversations throughout your day and creates high-level Apple Intelligence–generated summaries that you can use later to jog your memory, so you can stay present in the moment. Your summaries auto-delete after 7 days if you choose not to save them.

Siri Recap seems like the kind of feature that no one was necessarily asking for, but it could add valuable utility if the privacy protections are done right. You can read the finer details around privacy in Apple’s white paper here.

Live Rewind is another ‘Audio Intelligence’ feature coming to the new Apple Watch models later this year. It provides a more direct way to revisit something that was just said.
