title: Amazon Echo Smart Speakers Now Have Cameras, Wi-Fi Extenders and Home Hubs Built in
snippet: The preeminent smart speaker just got a little smarter – and more expensive.
fullText:
At the heart of the Echo smart speaker lineup are the Echo Dot, which brings simple smart home convenience, and the Echo Studio, Amazon’s premium listening speaker with a richer sound. Both got upgrades: the Dot now includes a built-in smart home hub and Wi-Fi extender, while a new version of the Studio adds a camera for live in-home monitoring (you can still buy the Echo Studio without a camera).

Amazon dropped a healthy slate of new and updated smart home devices this week, including a revamped Echo Show, its first-ever smart photo frame, and an alarm clock that apparently knows when you’re in a deep sleep and automatically snoozes the alarm so you can rest longer.

We got a sneak peek at the new smart home speakers at Amazon’s launch event.David Carnoy/CNET

The first Echo smart speaker with a built-in camera

Cameras are making their way into products they have no logical business being in, like dishwashers, but a camera in the $250 Echo Studio with Home Camera turns the humble smart speaker into a useful nanny cam, letting you keep tabs on family and pets via its live view. If you’re deciding between a pet cam and a smart speaker, the Echo device should offer a reliable version of both.

			

More from CNET

The cam does more than let you watch the dog chew slippers 

The Studio Home Camera serves as a nanny cam and uses adaptive vision to help with small tasks.David Carnoy/CNET

Through the Home Camera, Alexa “gains visual intelligence to make everyday experiences more personal and helpful,” according to Amazon. Alexa can “see and understand what’s in front of the camera and help. Pull out a board game box and ask Alexa to explain the rules or hold up a cereal box and Alexa can recognize it and help you reorder more flavors.”

Adaptive sound and volume for tailored listening

Camera shamera, the Echo Studio also has fancy new audio features.David Carnoy/CNET

Expect the same souped-up sound quality that Studio built its name on, including a high-excursion woofer for deep, immersive bass, three optimally placed full-range drivers, and Dolby Atmos to fill the room with immersive spatial audio. 

	

			

	

			

									

						The Best Smart Speakers We Tested					

							

		

A new feature called Advanced Room Adaptation adjusts the sound to your space’s unique acoustics, while Adaptive Volume adjusts the volume based on how close or far you are from the device. The latter sounds particularly useful for those of us who doddle about the house cooking and cleaning while trying to follow a podcast or audiobook.

Echo Dot is now a smart home hub and Wi-Fi extender

The smaller Echo Dot gets its own updates, including a smart home hub feature and a built-in Wi-Fi extender. 

For the first time, Amazon has integrated a smart home hub to connect and control compatible devices like your smart thermostat, lights and locks without the need for a standalone hub. The latest iteration adds a built-in Eero Wi-Fi extender that extends internet coverage by up to 1,000 square feet to an existing Eero network. 

For the first time, the Echo Dot features a built-in smart home hub and Wi-Fi extender.David Carnoy/CNET

Echo Dot is now powered by AZ3, Amazon’s custom-designed silicon, enabling advanced on-device

processing for faster, more natural conversations with Alexa Plus. Speaking of Alexa, there’s now a fourth speaker (all the better to hear you with, my dear).

Echo Dot and Studio pricing

Echo Studio with Home Camera is $249.99 and available in Graphite. An optional stand is sold separately for $39.99

Echo Dot is available in Graphite, Glacier White, Agave Green, and Coral Pink for $99.99.

Amazon Kids Echo Dot is available in two colorful designs – Octopus and Penguin – starting at $109.99

title: Apple responds to reports of iPhone Duo’s inner display cracking
snippet: Over the weekend, a handful of iPhone Duo users reported that their inner display had cracked along the hinge. In a statement to 9to5Mac, Apple said it is “aware of an issue impacting the inner display on a small number of iPhone Duo units,” and that affected users can contact AppleCare for a replacement. more…
fullText:
Over the weekend, a handful of iPhone Duo users reported that their inner display had cracked along the hinge. In a statement to 9to5Mac, Apple said it is “aware of an issue impacting the inner display on a small number of iPhone Duo units,” and that affected users can contact AppleCare for a replacement. 

Here is Apple’s full statement: 

“The response to iPhone Duo from early users has been incredibly positive, and we are seeing exciting things from developers who are rapidly updating their apps to take advantage of its unique form factor. We are aware of an issue impacting the inner display on a small number of iPhone Duo units. If users experience issues with their iPhone Duo display, they should contact AppleCare for a replacement.”

The company says the problem affects a very small number of iPhone Duo units and appears to surface relatively quickly. Most iPhone Duo units are not affected. You do not need AppleCare+ to have your iPhone Duo replaced for this problem. If you bought from a carrier, you should contact AppleCare directly, not your carrier, to get your device replaced. 

Reports of the problem surfaced on Reddit and other forums over the weekend. Affected users report that the inner screens cracked along the center line of the hinge. While a number of user reports on Reddit showing the issue are legitimate, there have been a handful of fake AI-generated reports as well. 

The folks at iFixit have pointed to a few potential causes of the problems, with certain components potentially putting excessive pressure on the display.

title: Apple’s low-cost iPhone 18 details revealed by leaker
snippet: Apple reportedly plans to introduce a low-cost iPhone 18e next spring alongside iPhone 18 and iPhone Air 2. Here are the details on what to expect from iPhone 18e, per a new leak. more…
fullText:
Apple reportedly plans to introduce a low-cost iPhone 18e next spring alongside iPhone 18 and iPhone Air 2. Here are the details on what to expect from iPhone 18e, per a new leak.

iPhone 18e will feature A20 chip and possible front camera upgrade, but remain very similar to iPhone 17e per leaker

When Apple introduced new iPhones last month, only three models launched: iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max, plus iPhone Duo.

Rumors indicate three more new iPhones are coming in early 2027: iPhone 18e, iPhone 18, and iPhone Air 2.

There’s been plenty of reporting on iPhone Air 2 changes, and some on the base iPhone 18, but surprisingly little on the entry-model iPhone 18e.

But today, a new post from Weibo leaker Digital Chat Station outlines what to expect from iPhone 18e early next year. He says it will feature:

60Hz display, meaning no ProMotion still

A20 chip, which doesn’t yet exist in non-Pro form

6.12-inch OLED like its predecessor

48MP single rear camera

Front camera “may be upgraded to 24MP”

Based on these specs, it sounds like iPhone 18e is focused largely on performance improvements.

The A20 chip will be interesting to evaluate, since we haven’t yet seen a non-Pro variant of the latest 2nm technology. Mention of a front camera upgrade is particularly surprising, but my guess is that if it does emerge, it will actually be an 18MP sensor like what’s in other models today.

Other than these two changes, every spec mentioned remains unchanged from iPhone 17e. One detail not addressed is whether the notch will be replaced by a Dynamic Island.

Considering the skyrocketing prices of memory and storage, and Apple’s aims to keep iPhone 18e a budget-friendly model, perhaps the new model will offer fewer upgrades than usual to keep costs down.

title: OnePlus starts rolling out stable Android 17 updates early, marking the end of OxygenOS
snippet: OnePlus is now rolling out stable Android 17 updates to OnePlus 15 and OnePlus Pad 4, marking the end of OxygenOS as these devices are just the first to transition to ColorOS. more…
fullText:
OnePlus is now rolling out stable Android 17 updates to OnePlus 15 and OnePlus Pad 4, marking the end of OxygenOS as these devices are just the first to transition to ColorOS.

OxygenOS has been OnePlus’ skin on top of Android for years. It started off as a “stock” skin with some added features, but eventually transitioned into a global-optimized version of Oppo’s ColorOS. So it wasn’t a surprise that, when OnePlus shut down most of its global operations, it was also announced that OxygenOS would go away with existing devices updating to ColorOS. 

Starting in India, ColorOS 17 based on Android 17 is rolling out to the OnePlus 15 and OnePlus Pad 4. The update has been in beta for a while now, but today marks the start of the stable rollout.

OnePlus summarizes ColorOS 17, saying:

	

ColorOS 17 is here, bringing a new wave of smarter experiences, smoother interactions, and more ways to make your phone work around you… At the heart of ColorOS 17 is an idea we believe in: Flow with AI, Flow Everywhere. Technology should feel less like something you have to figure out and more like something that naturally keeps up with you. From making everyday interactions feel more fluid to turning ideas into finished work with AI, we’re bringing intelligence closer to the moments that matter, helping you move between tasks, devices, and experiences with less friction.

Originally, OnePlus’ timeline put the first updates on October 29.

Other devices confirmed to be updated include last-gen flagships and an assortment of Nord devices, but OnePlus 15 and Pad 4 are the only two for this first wave. Presumably, the update will expand to other regions in the coming days. The next wave lands on October 30 and includes OnePlus 13.

title: Google Messages rolling out Enhanced Protection mode against spam and scams
snippet: Following the announcement earlier this month, Google Messages for Android is rolling out an Enhanced Protection mode to counter spam and scams. more…
fullText:
Following the announcement earlier this month, Google Messages for Android is rolling out an Enhanced Protection mode to counter spam and scams.

To date, Google Messages has offered Standard Protection to block “spam and suspected harmful links.” Enhanced Protection introduces “Advanced detection to prevent spam and scams.” There are three core features at launch.

Scam Detection will leverage “cloud Gemini models to evaluate complex message context and understand a scammer’s intent more quickly when you’re in a conversation with an unknown sender.” Compared to the existing on-device detection, this approach is better at identifying “novel and sophisticated attacks.”

It uses Android’s Private AI Compute feature to encrypt messages and process them in a secure space that is “private to you and not available to anyone else, including Google.”

	

Meanwhile, enhanced link protections use the on-device Gemini Nano model and real-time web signals to evaluate whether an unfamiliar link is trustworthy before you tap. This feature is available on the Pixel 10+, Samsung Galaxy S26 series, Z Flip 8, Z Fold 8, and “other select devices.”

	

The final update redesigns warnings to give you additional time and more context to “pause before tapping links” sent by numbers not in your contacts.

Enhanced Protection is an opt-in feature. To enable, go to Google Messages settings > Protection & safety. Instead of an on/off toggle, you’ll find three options:

Enhanced protection

Standard protection

No protection (not recommended)

We’re seeing this available with the latest Google Messages beta (version 20261020_00_RC00).

title: New iPad mini vs previous model: Here’s everything new
snippet: Apple unveiled a new iPad mini today, and it’s a big upgrade over the previous model. Here’s everything new. more…
fullText:
Apple unveiled a new iPad mini today, and it’s a big upgrade over the previous model. Here’s everything new.

Design: Thinner, reduced bezels, camera repositioned, and new colors

The new iPad mini look similar to the previous model, but also fresh and more modern thanks to two main design changes:

It’s thinner than ever, with a depth of 5.4mm compared to 6.3mm on the last model

Bezels are now 24% smaller than before

You may or may not notice, but the new mini is also slightly more narrow, measuring 132.6mm wide vs 134.8mm. And it weighs less: 255 grams vs 293 for Wi-Fi models.

The front-facing Center Stage camera is now positioned on the landscape side of the device rather than portrait.

Apple now offers the iPad mini in two colors: Midnight and Starlight. Previously more options were available, including Space Gray and Starlight, but the latest colors still have an updated look.

Display: Larger display with OLED, optional nano-texture

Thanks to the reduced bezels, the new iPad mini now has a larger, 8.5-inch display. The previous model’s was only 8.3 inches.

Perhaps a more significant change is that the display is OLED, a big upgrade from the LCD technology used before. Apple says this enables “pixel-level lighting control for much deeper blacks and support for the P3 wide color gamut for more vivid and accurate imagery.”

The display gets much brighter than before too, with peak brightness of 1200 nits, double the previous max of 600. Standard SDR and HDR brightness is 600 nits, up from 500. It also supports 1-nit minimum brightness for use in dim environments.

Apple now lets you optionally choose a nano-texture display on 256GB models and up. iPad mini has never previously offered nano-texture.

Performance: A20 Pro vs A17 Pro

The new iPad mini has an A20 Pro chip, Apple’s most powerful mobile processor that first debuted in iPhone 18 Pro and iPhone Duo. The previous generation had an A17 Pro. Per Apple:

A20 Pro delivers a giant leap in performance for iPad mini, significantly boosting graphics and AI-intensive tasks. It is built using Apple’s latest 2-nanometer process technology and a new package inspired by M-series chips. Powered by a 7-core GPU with Neural Accelerators in each GPU core, iPad mini delivers up to 4.5x faster AI performance than the previous generation — perfect for AI tasks ranging from running on-device models in creative apps to running local LLMs. And with the latest graphics architecture, including dynamic caching and hardware-accelerated mesh shading and ray tracing, graphics performance jumps by up to 2.7x — great for gaming and 3D rendering. A20 Pro also features up to a 6-core CPU for up to 60 percent faster multithreaded performance for everyday tasks like editing photos and working across apps.

A20 Pro also brings 2x increase in unified memory bandwidth.

One key detail worth noting is that the new iPad mini uses a binned A20 Pro chip in all but the high-end 512GB model. Not only does the binned chip have only 5 CPU cores rather than 6, it also lacks the Dual 16-core Neural Engine. Instead, you get the standard 16-core Neural Engine.

So if you’re comparing performance, Apple’s “up to” quotes refer to the 512GB model.

Acoustic Display speakers and IP67 water and dust resistance

Instead of the previous traditional stereo speaker setup, the new iPad mini uses “an innovative Acoustic Display” for audio, which Apple says delivers:

an even better audio experience when gaming, watching videos, or editing content. Specially designed woofers are paired through the display to produce punchier bass and more volume. In addition, custom tweeters are now hidden between the glass and aluminum enclosure for clearer highs.

The Acoustic Display has a sealed enclosure which enables iPad mini to offer IP67 water and dust resistance. This makes it more versatile than before.

Wireless connectivity, fast charging, and more

Apple’s N1 and C2 chips comes to the iPad mini, enabling the following connectivity improvements:

New iPad mini

Previous iPad mini

Wi-Fi

Wi-Fi 7

Wi-Fi 6E

Bluetooth

Bluetooth 6

Bluetooth 5.3

Cellular

Apple C2

Qualcomm

Additionally, though Apple didn’t give specific fast charging details for its last iPad mini, the new model supports: “Up to 50% charge in 30 minutes with a 35W adapter or higher.”

Finally, Apple also notes that the new iPad mini “supports extended display mode when connected to an external display, great for users multitasking with windowed apps.” Previously only mirroring was available, whereas this sounds like a full-fledged extended display feature.

Pricing and availability

	

As with nearly every other product these days, the iPad mini is getting more expensive with today’s updates. It now starts at $699, up from the previous $599 starting price. 

Pre-orders for the new iPad mini will open this Wednesday, October 28 at 10:10 a.m. PT and orders deliver on Friday, November 6.

title: New iPhone Duo? Here are 4 Cool Features to Try
snippet: A handful of neat capabilities help Apple’s foldable phone feel even more intuitive.
fullText:
If you’ve managed to snag a shiny new iPhone Duo, congratulations on surviving the scramble to get one. Now the fun begins.

I’ve spent two weeks with Apple’s first foldable phone, and it has several features that make it feel like a genuinely practical and intuitive device — and with a $1,999 starting price, I’d sure hope so. 

What stands out about the Duo is its versatility. Similar to other passport-size folding phones like the Samsung Galaxy Z Fold 8 and the Xiaomi 18 Fold, you can hop between a more compact, 5.4-inch cover screen when sending a text or checking a notification and a wider, 7.6-inch inner display when watching videos, multitasking or scrolling through social media. It’s like a phone-tablet hybrid that fits neatly into a pocket or the palm of your hand. 

		

			

Details like the matte inner display, which minimizes glare and makes the crease less noticeable, along with seamless software integration across screens give the Duo a distinct character of its own.

Here are four features worth checking out to get the most of your new iPhone Duo. And if you’re still in the market for one, it’s worth checking out carrier and trade-in deals to help bring down the cost (and maybe get the phone earlier than January).

Use Duo Preview and Smart Take for photos

Smart Take and Duo Preview can make taking photos a little easier.Abrar Al-Heeti/CNET

The iPhone Duo’s foldable design and dual screens open up more ways to take pictures. A few handy features let you easily use the 48-megapixel rear cameras for better shots than you’d get with the 12-megapixel cover-screen selfie camera.

If someone is taking a picture of you or you want to snap a selfie with the rear camera, use Duo Preview to get a glimpse of what the shot will look like. With the phone open, you’ll see an image preview on the cover screen as you or your photographer snaps away, so you can ensure the framing and poses look exactly how you want.

To turn on Duo Preview, unfold the Duo and open the Camera app. Then tap the control in the top left corner (when the phone is in landscape) that looks like a mini Duo. Tap Duo Preview and snap away. 

If you’re trying to take a group photo and there’s no one around to snap it for you, you no longer have to awkwardly prop your phone against a surface and then race against a timer — or make do with a lackluster selfie. Place your Duo on a flat surface when it’s half-folded and point the camera at your subjects. A feature called Smart Take will use AI to detect when everyone is in-frame and ready, and then automatically take a photo. As people change their poses, Smart Take will register that there’s a fresh scene to snap. You can also use Duo Preview to check framing via the cover screen.

To enable Smart Take, open the camera app while the Duo is either opened or closed. Then tap the photo options in the corner (six little dots), and tap Smart Take. A button with a yellow circle will then appear to the right of the shutter; tap that to start the process. 

Smart Take will keep snapping pictures for around two minutes or until it captures about 20 images as people readjust their poses. You’ll then be able to sift through the options in Photos. 

Lastly, Kid Cue can make it easier to hold a child’s attention when snapping photos. With the Duo open, a Snoopy animation will play on the cover screen to draw attention toward the camera. To turn on Kid Cue, unfold the Duo, open the Camera app and tap the Duo icon in the upper left corner. There, you’ll see the option to turn on Kid Cue. 

StandBy mode gets more handy

StandBy on the iPhone Duo works even when the phone isn’t charging.Abrar Al-Heeti/CNET

Apple launched StandBy in 2023, which turns the iPhone into a smart display of sorts, with access to widgets like the clock, calendar and weather. But unlike other iPhones, the Duo doesn’t have to be charging to launch into StandBy. 

Just set the Duo down while it’s locked, either slightly unfolded and on its side in tent mode, or while standing upright. Then you’ll see your favorite widgets, as well as Live Activities. That way, you can track the status of a food delivery, sports score or approaching rideshare at a glance.  

To ensure StandBy is enabled, go to your iPhone’s Settings, then tap StandBy and check that the toggle is on.

Marathon watch as you like

Netflix is optimized for the Duo’s displays — from the cover screen to the main display to this half-open configuration with controls on the bottom half. Celso Bulgatti/CNET

Streaming video really shines with the iPhone Duo’s dynamic design. Open the phone to watch on the tablet-like, 7.6-inch display. Minimal black bars at the top and bottom of the screen allow for more immersive viewing. 

You can also fold the Duo halfway and set it down, essentially making it look like a mini laptop. With apps like Netflix and Apple TV, your movie or TV show will play on the top half, while controls appear on the bottom for skipping forward, rewinding, pausing, playing and turning on closed captions. Netflix also has an added flair: You’ll see what appears to be a reflection of the upper-screen’s content playing down by the controls, as if it’s subtly mirroring that footage. It makes for a nifty immersive effect.

You can also prop your iPhone Duo into tent mode and watch content on the 5.4-inch cover screen. I do this when I’m moving around my apartment tidying up. That way, I can easily see what’s happening without needing a phone stand. Even though the Duo’s cover screen is significantly smaller than the main display, it’s just big enough to still comfortably watch most content (perhaps not as Christopher Nolan intended, but it’ll do). 

Lock a pair of apps when multitasking

You can lock an app pair when multitasking. Celso Bulgatti/CNET

The iPhone Duo can run up to two apps simultaneously in its open horizontal orientation, so you can watch a YouTube video on one half of your screen while texting your friends on the other, for example. Some other foldable phones support running three apps side-by-side, but I find that feels too crowded. 

On the iPhone Duo, you can save an app pair, so that if you swipe away, you can quickly pull up that same combination without having to drag the apps side by side again. It’s a quick time-saver that lends itself to the intuitive nature of iOS 27 on the iPhone Duo.

To create an app pair, tap the divider between two apps that you’ve already dragged side by side. This will lock in that combination, so you can easily restore that dual-window card when you’re scrolling through the App Switcher. Just select the still-paired window and carry on with your multitasking (or doomscrolling).

				

					

						

													

					

					

						

Abrar Al-Heeti
						

						

							Senior Technology Reporter

title: Google Wallet rolling out notifications feed, support for more digital passports [U]
snippet: After the stacked card list redesign, Google Wallet for Android is gaining a notifications feed and support for more passports. more…
fullText:
After the stacked card list redesign, Google Wallet for Android is gaining a notifications feed and support for more passports.

On the homepage, you’ll see a notification bell icon next to the profile switcher in the top-right corner. Tapping opens a feed with “updates about items in Wallet.” 

Earlier this month, the company said it was introducing an “in-app message center in Google Wallet.” This new feature is still rolling out via a server-side update.

Meanwhile, Google Wallet is adding support for more digital passports. Officially referred to as an “ID pass” in the app, usage varies by country. US passports can be used at TSA security via NFC or QR code scanning. 

	

Update 10/23: Following Brazil, Singapore, Taiwan, United Kingdom, and the United States of America, we’re starting to see the ability to add Estonia, Ireland, Italy, and Spain.

The new countries are not widely rolled out yet.

To add a passport, tap the ‘plus’ FAB at the bottom of Google Wallet > IDs & personal info > ID pass. The registration process involves scanning your passport info page and security chip. Afterward, you have to record a video of your face. You’ll get a notification once verification is complete.

title: Will Apple’s overhauled MacBook Pro finally offer 5G cellular support?
snippet: This week, Apple will be overhauling the MacBook Pro for the first time since 2021. OLED, touch support, and a significantly lighter design are expected. Another rumor for the new MacBook Pros has been cellular support, though it’s been unclear if that’s actually going to ship. more…
fullText:
This week, Apple will be overhauling the MacBook Pro for the first time since 2021. OLED, touch support, and a significantly lighter design are expected. Another rumor for the new MacBook Pros has been cellular support, though it’s been unclear if that’s actually going to ship.

To recap, Apple is expected to unveil its first touchscreen MacBooks at its ‘Pro and tell’ experience on October 28 in LA. It likely won’t be a streamed event, just a hands-on experience for influencers and media. At that event, we should be seeing the OLED iPad mini, OLED MacBook Pro, as well as a refreshed iMac and 14″ base model MacBook Pro, both with the M6 chip.

Cellular MacBook on the way?

If Apple were to ship a cellular MacBook, it would likely utilize the C2 modem seen in iPhone 18 Pro and iPhone Duo. Even though we don’t know for sure if this weeks new MacBooks will offer cellular, we have a number of hints to suggest so.

In 2024, Bloomberg’s Mark Gurman initially reported that Apple was investigating cellular MacBooks for as early as 2026. Back then, he reported that Apple was testing its second generation modem with these MacBooks, which we can assume is the C2.

Additionally, last year, Filipe Esposito reported at Macworld that Apple was testing configurations of an M5 Pro-based MacBook Pro with Apple’s C1 modem. Of course, this is just testing, but the fact that it was with an M5 Pro chip is interesting given the fact that these new MacBooks this week will debut with the M5 Pro and M5 Max chips, rather than M6-based chips.

Since then, we haven’t had any substantive leaks regarding cellular support in the MacBook Pro lineup. That said, we haven’t had any leaks explicitly ruling it out, either. One way or the other, it should only be a matter of days until we know for sure.

title: The new MacBook Pro has everything I wanted, minus one thing
snippet: Apple’s new MacBook Pro with PROLED XDR is an exciting upgrade that delivers nearly every feature I was hoping for, with just one exception. more…
fullText:
Apple’s new MacBook Pro with PROLED XDR is an exciting upgrade that delivers nearly every feature I was hoping for, with just one exception.

MacBook Pro with PROLED XDR is an exciting leap forward, and might replace the iPad Pro as my primary computer

I’ve been waiting a long time for the MacBook Pro with PROLED XDR. I haven’t used a Mac as my primary computer in years, but rumors about this new model made me think that might finally change.

The iPad Pro has been my main computer of choice since 2015, but lately I’ve grown increasingly curious about revisiting the Mac full-time.

This is largely due to Apple making the Mac, to me at least, a lot more exciting than it was in 2015. The Mac’s hardware and software are advancing in compelling new ways, and today’s new MacBook Pro brings an especially big leap.

As a longtime iPad Pro user, I’ve come to expect features like touch support and OLED in a relatively thin, lightweight device. I also love how iPadOS tends to advance in lockstep with iOS, a trend that has recently started extending to macOS too.

Until recently, it seemed like Apple’s latest and greatest tech—with the exception of pro-focused chips—has been in the iPad and iPhone.

I don’t need an extremely powerful chip, as my computing needs are pretty basic. But I do value having a great display, touch support, and modern OS features like the Dynamic Island.

The MacBook Pro with PROLED XDR delivers those things. I’ve ordered one and can’t wait to give it a legitimate shot to be my full-time computer. But my biggest hesitation is the lack of cellular.

The lack of cellular is my one MacBook Pro disappointment

I use cellular all the time on my iPad Pro. I tend to work from coffee shops and random outdoor spots for at least a few hours every day. And in my experience, public Wi-Fi options aren’t reliable enough for my needs.

Having a persistent cellular connection on my iPad is a killer feature. I very much wish Apple provided the option of cellular on the MacBook Pro too.

I’m hoping that personal hotspot has become a lot more reliable since I last tried it. Apple does say its N1 wireless chip makes the feature better. 

	

Additionally, I wonder if the need for cellular will be mitigated some by having a tablet-sized iPhone Duo in my pocket soon. So if I need to stop in the middle of nowhere and get work done quickly, maybe the Duo will suffice.

In any case, the MacBook Pro looks like a fantastic product regardless. It’s not for everyone, and the high price hurts, but I’m excited to give it a try.

title: Amazon’s $500 Echo Show 16 Wants to Be the Center of Your Home
snippet: A larger screen, upgraded speakers, night vision and an optional glare-resistant display headline Amazon’s latest Echo Show.
fullText:
Amazon is betting there’s room for another screen in your home, and that you’ll pay $500 for it.

The company announced the Echo Show 16 on Wednesday, a new 16-inch smart display that combines Alexa Plus, Fire TV and a customizable home dashboard into a single device. It starts at $500, with a $570 version featuring an anti-glare screen.

The Echo Show 16 is now available for preorder, with a $100 discount for early buyers. Amazon says the device will ship later this year, but hasn’t announced an exact date.

			

More from CNET

As CNET’s smart home expert Tyler Lacoma notes, Amazon is going in a very different direction than Apple this year.Amazon

The new smart display is designed to do a little bit of everything, whether that’s controlling lights, managing your family’s calendar, making video calls or streaming Netflix while you’re cooking dinner.

A bigger screen and an optional anti-glare upgrade

The Echo Show 16 has a full HD display that Amazon says offers 10% more viewing area than the Echo Show 15. It also has a redesigned aluminum frame that’s nearly 40% thinner than its predecessor, which could make it less obtrusive when mounted on a wall. A new 10-speaker system is designed to deliver fuller sound for music, TV shows and video calls.

One of the biggest additions is an optional Nanomatte display, which Amazon says reduces glare by more than 90%. That could make a difference if you’re using the Echo Show in a kitchen with bright overhead lighting or near a window.

Read more: Amazon’s New Echo Lineup Goes in the Opposite Direction of Apple HomeView

The Echo Show 16 also includes a 13-megapixel wide-angle camera for video calls, with automatic framing to keep people in the shot. Amazon says it more than doubles the range of Visual ID, which can recognize household members and personalize what’s on the screen, from 8 feet to 17 feet.

The Echo Show 16 is also the first in the lineup to offer night vision, letting you see what’s happening at home even in the dark.

Amazon says a dedicated button can disable the microphones and camera. That’s worth noting given previous concerns about changes to Alexa’s privacy settings.

A smart home dashboard that doubles as a TV

The Echo Show 16 is somewhere between a TV and a smart display.Amazon

Amazon is introducing three new screen styles that change how the Echo Show 16 home screen looks and functions. Smart Home turns the display into an always-on control center for connected devices, including lights, thermostats and speakers. Family Organizer brings together shared calendars, to-do lists, meal plans and recipes. Photos turns the screen into a digital photo frame.

There’s also a customizable favorites bar for quick access to frequently used features.

The Echo Show 16 comes with Fire TV built in, letting you stream content from services including Netflix, Disney Plus, YouTube and Prime Video. The box includes a remote, so you won’t have to rely entirely on voice commands or the touchscreen.

Fire TV is already available on the Echo Show 15 and 21, but the new customizable dashboards give the Echo Show 16 more ways to serve as a central home hub.

Alexa Plus gets a more visual experience

An upgraded display on the Echo Show 16 costs even more.Amazon

The Echo Show 16 also runs Amazon’s Alexa Plus AI assistant, which can handle more conversational requests and multi-step tasks. Alexa Plus isn’t exclusive to the new display, though. Amazon previously introduced Echo Show 8 and Echo Show 11 models designed for the upgraded assistant.

Instead of simply displaying a transcript of a conversation, the new interface can generate interactive content, including comparison charts, videos and recommendations, as you speak to Alexa.

Amazon is also introducing Cards, which organize previous Alexa conversations into topics you can revisit. For example, a conversation about planning a weekend trip could produce a Card containing relevant links, reservations and other details.

Certain features require Alexa Plus, which is included with a Prime membership. Without Prime, the full Alexa Plus experience costs $20 a month.

The Echo Show 16 costs $500 with the standard display or $570 with Nanomatte. Both versions are eligible for a $100 preorder discount. It doesn’t include a stand, so you’ll need to mount it on a wall or buy one separately. Amazon offers a $70 basic stand or a $125 swivel-and-tilt version.

For comparison, Amazon’s larger 21-inch Echo Show 21 launched in 2024 at $400. Add the Nanomatte display and swivel-and-tilt stand, and the Echo Show 16 comes to nearly $700 before taxes and the preorder discount. That’s a steep price for a smart display, even one that wants to double as a TV, family organizer and smart home hub.

Now, the popular accessory maker is back with Airfly View, which adds a built-in screen to its other popular wireless audio dongle. You can order it on Amazon today. Here’s how it works.

Use your own wireless headphones or earbuds with any headphone jack.

Built-in screen with step-by-step guided setup.

On-screen setup in 24 languages.

Connect two wireless headphones at once.

Zippered hard-shell travel case included.

International airline adapter included.

Up to 16 hours of battery life, with battery level shown on screen.

Works with seatbacks, gym equipment, cars, boats, and home stereos.

Auracast broadcast support.

title: What’s Faster Than an F1 Car? The Data Behind the Race
snippet: For diehard fans and newcomers like me, tech offers deeper insights into the race while helping broadcasters tell a richer story. I went behind the scenes to see how it all comes together.
fullText:
Technology has always been central to Formula One, but it’s playing an increasingly important role in how races are brought to fans around the world.

Ahead of the United States Grand Prix, which ran Friday through Sunday in Austin, Texas, I got a behind-the-scenes look at the on-site production facilities and how data is analyzed and turned into broadcast insights that help viewers – newcomers like me included – better understand the action unfolding on the track.

F1 has surged in popularity in the US in recent years, driven by factors like increased social media exposure, new race destinations and a more personal connection with drivers, thanks in part to Netflix’s hit docuseries Drive to Survive. And with cars reaching speeds of up to 230 miles per hour, it’s easy to see what makes the sport so thrilling.

			

More from CNET

But those cars aren’t just lightning-fast; they’re also data-gathering machines. Each F1 car generates around 1.1 million data points per second from 300 sensors. Technology partners like Amazon Web Services help process and analyze that information, turning complex data into insights that anyone, from casual viewers to die-hard data nerds, can understand and enjoy – including race metrics previously available only to production crews. 

F1 is all about high speeds and even faster data.Abrar Al-Heeti/CNET

Then there are people like me, somewhere in between — intrigued by the F1 frenzy but still learning the rules, technical details and strategies that keep millions of fans invested in every race. That’s where a handful of digital tools can help make sense of the fast-moving action, revealing the stories behind the numbers.

“To know a sport is to love a sport,” said Ruth Buscombe, technical adviser and race strategist at Formula One and AWS motorsports ambassador. “When you look at any kind of relationship you have with something that is a passion, it’s about starting as a novice and then learning about it and falling in love with the details of it. And sports has always been that.” 

Inside the Event Technical Centre, the backbone of F1’s global broadcast

Feeds from the on-track cameras and microphones go through F1’s Event Technical Centre before the footage makes its way on air.F1/AWS

Nestled behind the swanky Paddock Club and team hospitality units sits a white, temporary hangar-like facility called the F1 Event Technical Centre, or ETC. 

This hub is where data from across the circuit is brought together. Dozens of cameras and hundreds of microphones capture the sights and sounds of the race from almost every angle, while each car’s 300 sensors monitor everything from tire pressure to airspeed. For broadcast production, these feeds and data streams are then sent to F1’s Media & Technology Centre in Biggin Hill, UK.

Construction of the tent-like ETC, which spans 375 square meters (about 4,036 square feet), begins 10 days before the race and takes five days to complete. The process includes laying a network of over 58 kilometers (around 36 miles) of fiber-optic cables, as well as data antennas that enable two-way information transfer to and from the cars speeding around the track. 

Up to 28 ultra-high-definition trackside cameras capture the action, alongside cable cams, helicopters, drones, free-roaming cameras and slow-motion cameras. More than 90 cameras are mounted directly on the cars, with up to eight views available from each. The 150 microphones positioned around the circuit capture the quintessential sounds of an F1 race, from the roar of the engines to the screech of the tires (now coming in clear to viewers with Dolby Atmos on Apple TV, along with Dolby Vision).

Inside the ETC, around 140 technical, operations and TV production crew members work side by side, surrounded by glowing switchboards, computer screens and monitors displaying the on-track action, including close-up shots of the cars and sweeping aerial views of the circuit.

The ETC houses around 750 pieces of equipment, according to F1.F1/AWS

In one room, timekeepers track lap times to within one ten-thousandth of a second, with additional timekeepers based at the UK’s Media & Technology Centre. Behind them, teams process and relay data from cameras, audio feeds and car sensors to their headquarters in Europe to support real-time strategy decisions. Sensors positioned around the track every 150 meters also help with vehicle tracking and positioning maps, as well as monitoring potential violations, such as speeding in the pit lane. An operations team at the back ensures the ETC and UK command center are in sync.

In another room, directors decide which shots to use and when to cut to replays or add graphics, which are also handled by team members in this area. A separate crew monitors the team radio, which is delayed by around 20 seconds so they can add subtitles and, importantly, bleep out any swear words.

At the far end of the ETC, a wall of routers and servers transmits the live camera feeds, audio and data to the UK’s Media & Technology Centre. There, production teams turn those feeds into the international broadcast watched by around 1.6 billion viewers.

“We have this really diverse fan base, and we have a complicated story to tell,” said Dean Locke, executive director of broadcast at Formula One. It’s not just the fan base that’s diverse, but also the ways people tune in – whether they’re watching on a big screen, a tablet or a phone.

“The way we develop graphics, the way we develop footage, that is something that we keep in mind,” Locke said. “Is it hitting every single fan?”

Giving fans deeper insights with Track Pulse

Formula One partnered with AWS in 2018, moving much of its computing infrastructure from on-premises data centers to the cloud. AWS also helps F1 refine race strategies, improve digital broadcasts and collect and analyze data, of which there is plenty. 

Now, F1 and AWS are making Track Pulse, a tool the broadcast team has used since 2023, available to fans for the first time this season. 

Track Pulse sifts through vast amounts of data from each car’s sensors to highlight the moments and decisions that can shape a race. From sudden changes in pace to shifting weather conditions to tire strategies, these callouts can help viewers better understand not just what’s happening on track but also why it matters. 

“It’s near impossible to have enough pairs of eyes to monitor all 22 cars at the same time and really pick up on the small details of what’s happening,” said Jerome Descreux, AWS senior engagement manager. That’s why broadcast teams have been using Track Pulse to help determine what to spotlight for viewers. And now, viewers can tap into those insights themselves via F1’s data channel, whether they’re watching in the US through Apple TV or internationally with an F1 TV Pro or Premium subscription. 

Track Pulse can offer more in-depth insights into what’s unfolding on track, giving viewers a heads-up on what to look out for and why.AWS

The interface is a data-rich dashboard with developing “stories,” as they’re called, on the left side, such as when a driver is quickly catching up to another. Track Pulse also displays live team radio transcripts, allowing viewers to peek into the conversations impacting the race. The goal is to distill the endless raw data into elements viewers may be interested in exploring and following.  

For instance, during the 2026 Australian Grand Prix, Track Pulse flagged a moment when George Russell rapidly closed the gap between him and Lewis Hamilton. The tool highlighted this point because of just how quickly Russell was catching up. Track Pulse also noted that Hamilton was using the same tires for an unusually long time, giving fans further insight into the decisions shaping the action on track. 

“We need to make sure that we’re bringing our fans on the journey,” said Formula One IT Director Chris Roberts. “For those people that are really technical, we’re not dulling things down so that it’s a bit boring for them, but also for those fans that are on a learning journey, we’re giving them the information that allows them to understand the sport at different levels.”

Most people might not get the chance to sit trackside, but data feeds for viewers at home can make the action feel closer.Abrar Al-Heeti/CNET

On the broadcast side, Track Pulse’s AI insights complement the F1 production team’s work, helping them sift through millions of data points to identify key race moments and turn them into digestible insights for people hungry to understand more of the action.

“We originally designed [Track Pulse] to be a producer’s tool,” Locke said. “Then we realized the power of it as a storytelling device. And it could crunch data and create story cards and tell us things that are going on in the races that even an entrenched producer of 20 years wasn’t seeing.”

He added, “Once someone gets into Formula One, they realize how much depth there is, and I think Track Pulse explains it quite well.”

Getting deeper insights with AI  

Insights powered by AWS can help distill the fast-moving action on the track.AWS

AWS also powers around two dozen data-driven F1 Insights, as they’re called, which add real-time analysis to live broadcasts. One example is the Battle Forecast, which estimates how many laps it might take for a chasing car to get close enough to attempt an overtake. The prediction is based on information like track history and projected driver pace, giving viewers a better sense of when the action could heat up.

Tire Performance is another insight that helps fans understand how different driving styles affect tire longevity and how tire condition can influence pit stop timing. And Close to the Wall uses specialized cameras and deep neural network algorithms to track a car’s trajectory in real time and calculate just how close it is to a wall, since even a slight brush at high speeds can affect lap times or damage the car’s carbon-fiber components.

Today, fans can essentially tap into the same data that teams and strategists have long used to gain even the slightest edge over their competitors.

On-screen blurbs can help viewers understand why a team made a particular decision.AWS

“[Teams and strategists] have been doing this for 70 years before anybody at home got to see it,” Buscombe said. “And now, AWS is using the exact same data, doing the exact same math, creating the exact same insights. But rather than it just being a black box where the Formula One teams get to have all the fun, now you, as a fan sitting on your sofa – whether it’s your first race or your 1,000th – you get to see the same kind of data. And those are the F1 insights that pop up on screen.”

Tech and data are set to play an even bigger role in the sport, particularly with AWS now serving as the official AI and cloud computing partner of the FIA, Formula One’s governing body. The partnership could influence everything from race operations to the design of future cars. Running aerodynamic simulations using AWS cloud computing, for instance, allows the FIA to virtually test how air flows around a car without building physical components, which can potentially speed up development.

This past weekend was my first foray into the world of F1, but the combination of technology, data and high-speed racing has already piqued my interest. I may still have plenty to learn, but at least I have some tools to help me make sense of it all.

Editors’ note: Abrar Al-Heeti’s travel costs for the F1 United States Grand Prix in Austin were covered by AWS. The judgments and opinions of CNET are our own.

				

					

						

													

					

					

						

Abrar Al-Heeti
						

						

							Senior Technology Reporter						
					

											

								

											Abrar's interests include phones, streaming, autonomous vehicles, internet trends, entertainment, pop culture and digital accessibility. In addition to her current role, she's worked for CNET's video, culture and news teams. She graduated with bachelor's and master's degrees in journalism from the University of Illinois at Urbana-Champaign. Though Illinois is home, she now loves San Francisco -- steep inclines and all.

title: Who will you learn from in 6 days at TechCrunch Founder Summit? Meet the founders and investors taking the stages
snippet: Six days from now, TechCrunch Founder Summit brings experienced founders, investors, and operators to Boston on Nov. 4 to share the decisions, mistakes, pivots, and lessons that shaped their companies. Register before it starts for ticket savings and deals.
fullText:
There are plenty of places to find startup advice. TechCrunch Founder Summit is about hearing what happened when people actually put that advice to the test.

Six days from now, TechCrunch Founder Summit, presented by Fidelity Private Shares, brings experienced founders, investors, and operators to Boston to share the decisions, mistakes, pivots, and lessons that shaped their companies. 

Register now to save up to $100, get a second ticket free when you buy one, or save up to 30% on group ticket bundles. Don’t miss these deals before the event starts on November 4.

Who and what are on the agenda

Explore the full Founder Summit agenda to discover the breakout and roundtable sessions and speakers bringing actionable insights, hard-earned lessons, and practical advice to help you scale your startup.

Image Credits:Halo Creative / Flickr (opens in a new window)

From Boston startup to public company

Few stories capture the potential of the Boston startup ecosystem better than Toast.

Steve Fredette, president, co-founder, and director of Toast, will talk about what it takes to keep reinventing a company even after the original idea works.

Scaling creates a new set of questions: How do you keep innovating? How do you stay close to the customers who got you there? And how do you evolve as technology and expectations change around you?

For founders trying to move from early traction toward meaningful scale, those are the questions that matter.

Know whether you’re actually ready to grow

Growth can be exciting. Premature growth can be expensive. Kent Bennett, Partner at Bessemer Venture Partners, will explore how founders can recognize meaningful product-market fit before they scale.

Rudina Seseri, Founder and Managing Partner of Glasswing Ventures, will take that conversation further by tackling when founders should accelerate and when hitting the brakes may be the smarter decision.

Together, those sessions give founders perspectives from both sides of the growth equation.

Build better teams, pitches, and companies

The agenda goes well beyond fundraising. Vineet Edupuganti of Cogent Security will explore how founders can build exceptional teams.

Dave Balter of True Ventures and Edisyl will focus on the pitch and why a founder’s goal isn’t to explain everything in one meeting. It’s to make someone want the next one.

Chase Garbarino of HqO will bring the conversation home with a look at what it takes to build and scale an ambitious company from Boston.

And Tina Tosukhowong of TDK Ventures will explore the signals investors look for when evaluating potential category leaders.

One day. A lot of experience in one room.

TechCrunch Founder Summit gives attendees access to people who have built companies, funded them, scaled them, hired through growth, sold into large enterprises, and made difficult calls when the right answer wasn’t obvious. Come with questions. Leave with perspectives you can actually use.

title: Samsung’s new Fitbit competitor just leaked [Video]
snippet: Samsung has a new Galaxy Fit 4 fitness tracker in the works, and it looks just a bit more like an Apple Watch this time around. more…
fullText:
Samsung has a new Galaxy Fit 4 fitness tracker in the works, and it looks just a bit more like an Apple Watch this time around.

The Galaxy Fit lineup serves as a more affordable alternative to the Galaxy Watch series, offering a smaller, less advanced wearable that still serves core functions in fitness tracking and providing a clock face. The latest release was 2024’s Galaxy Fit 3 and it seems Samsung has a new refresh incoming.

Leaked images from The Cipher Project on Telegram give us a pretty good look at the Galaxy Fit 4 in three colors. The hardware itself isn’t all that different from Fit 3, but there’s certainly another half-step into Apple Watch territory this time, especially with the other two color variants and the adjustment to the curve in the watch band.

Android Authority also managed to uncover a video of the tracker, showing the band mechanism and sensors on the back. 

	

The Galaxy Fit 4 will have to face off against Google’s Fitbit Edge upon launch, whenever it might arrive, though its not-so-secret weapon could be pricing. Galaxy Fit 3 was just $60 when it made its debut in the US, and still sells for less than that even though Samsung has ended first-party sales.

title: Google Photos rolls out customizable redesign of your ‘Collections’ tab
snippet: Following the floating navigation bar in July, Google Photos is rolling out a big redesign that lets you customize the Collections tab on Android and iOS. more…
fullText:
Following the floating navigation bar in July, Google Photos is rolling out a big redesign that lets you customize the Collections tab on Android and iOS.

The previous design started with a 2×2 grid. Favorites and Trash were at the top, while the other two shortcuts changed based on usage. Then there were large cards for Albums, On this device, People & pets, Wardrobe, Documents, Places, Stickers, and Moments. On Android, this was followed by a list: Screenshots, Videos, Recently Added, Archive, and Locked.

Old

This redesign of Collections is focused on customization. The first section is called “Pinned” and lets you choose which cards appear. By default, the carousel shows Favorites, Screenshots, and Trash. You also have the option to remove this section entirely. 

	
	

That’s followed by carousels for On this device, Albums, People & pets, Wardrobe, Places, and Documents. “View all” at the top-right corner lets you jump straight to the full grid or list view. Other options let you hide each section and rearrange the order in which they appear.

New

The “Other Collections” grid rounds out this page: Favorites, Screenshots, Moments, Videos, Recently Added, Stickers, Creations, Archive, Locked, and Trash. The “Reorder” button is found at the very bottom. 

This redesign is now widely rolling out with Google Photos 7.97 (Android) and 7.98 (iOS). Instead of the usual Force stop on Android, we’ve curiously been able to get this server-side update by restarting our devices and then opening the Photos app.

And there’s an additional bonus for anyone looking to give Craft a try: 40% off for life with code 9to5Mac40, available through this exclusive 9to5Mac offer.

From quick notes to big ideas: Craft on iPhone Duo

Craft has always been developed specifically for Apple’s platforms, with the same features available across iPhone, iPad, and Mac, but an interface tailored to each device. That approach carries over to iPhone Duo, where Craft adapts between compact and unfolded poses.

In its compact form, Craft works much like it does on any other iPhone. You can quickly capture an idea, check off a task, or work on a document with the full set of editing and formatting tools. Unfold the device, though, and there’s suddenly much more room to work with. Writing, organizing information, and navigating longer documents all benefit from the additional space. The matte inner display with its nano-texture finish is particularly well suited to reading, especially when browsing through Craft’s richly styled documents.

The larger display is also a good fit for some of Craft’s more advanced features. Collections, for example, let you organize information in structured views, including Tables and Kanban boards. Being able to see more cards and information at once makes these views considerably more useful on the unfolded screen.

One of the Duo specific iOS features that has gotten the most praise from reviewers is the new side-by-side multitasking mode, and it’s particularly useful with Craft. You can keep a document open on one side of the screen and Photos on the other, dragging images directly into your document. Or open Safari alongside Craft to drag over text, images, and even entire web pages while researching a topic or putting together a mood board.

It’s a good example of how the new form factor can make familiar workflows feel quite different, without requiring an entirely new way of using the app.

Built for the entire Apple ecosystem

For those unfamiliar with Craft, it’s a productivity app that brings notes, tasks, and documents together in one place. You can capture ideas, organize projects, plan your day, and create polished documents to share with others, all within the same app.

Craft is available on iPhone, iPad, Mac, and even Apple Vision Pro, with fast syncing that makes it easy to move between devices. It’s also built to work offline, so you can keep writing or organizing your notes on the subway or during a flight. Your changes sync automatically once you’re connected again.

But Craft’s approach goes beyond making the same app available everywhere. Its interface and interactions are designed for each platform, whether you’re working with touch on an iPhone or using a keyboard and trackpad on a Mac. One of Craft’s strengths is how easy it makes it to create good-looking documents, without having to spend much time adjusting layouts or formatting. And if you want to share your work, you can turn any document into a website with a single click.

And of course, being so deeply integrated into the Apple ecosystem, Craft takes full advantage of Apple’s OS features. Home Screen and Lock Screen widgets keep frequently used content within reach, Shortcuts lets you automate common workflows, and Siri AI makes it possible to access and work with your Craft content without always having to open the app.

Craft keeps getting better, wherever you use it

While the iPhone Duo launch is a good reason to take another look at Craft, quite a bit has changed in the app itself over the past few months. Rather than focusing exclusively on adding new features, the Craft team has spent much of the summer revisiting existing ones, improving how they work and making everyday interactions faster and more consistent.

The team started by revisiting tasks. In Craft, tasks can live directly inside your notes and documents, keeping them close to the information they’re related to. At the same time, dedicated task views bring everything together, so you can see what’s due today, plan upcoming work, and keep track of tasks across different projects without having to open each document individually.

Templates have also become more flexible. You can start with one of Craft’s existing templates or create your own for recurring workflows, whether that’s meeting notes, project plans, or weekly reflections. You can now also assign a default template to your Daily Notes, so every new day starts with the structure you’ve chosen.

Another area where Craft has taken a somewhat different approach is AI. Rather than making it central to every interaction, Craft treats AI as an optional tool that users can incorporate into their workflow as much or as little as they like.

Craft Assistant is built into the app and can help with writing, editing, and working with information in your documents. You can use it through Craft’s built-in credit system or connect your own AI provider using Bring Your Own Key (BYOK). For those who prefer working with external AI tools, Craft also supports MCP, making it possible to connect your documents and tasks to other agents and build more customized workflows.

And if you’d rather not use AI at all, you can simply disable the assistant in Settings. Unlike some productivity apps that are increasingly building their entire experience around AI, Craft isn’t pushing AI into every interaction, forcing you to change how you work, or making you pay more for features you never asked for. Whether you use its built-in assistant, bring your own provider, or turn AI off entirely, the choice remains yours.

A good time to try Craft

With a new experience on iPhone Duo and a long list of improvements across iPhone, iPad, and Mac, Craft has plenty to offer both new and returning users. Whether you’re looking to organize your notes and tasks or create documents that are easy to share, there’s quite a bit worth exploring.

And there’s an additional incentive for anyone looking to give Craft a try: 40% off for life with code 9to5Mac40, available through the exclusive 9to5Mac offer.

title: HomePod 27.2 is available now with four new features
snippet: Apple has released HomePod 27.2, its latest software update for HomePod users. Here’s what’s new. more…
fullText:
Apple has released HomePod 27.2, its latest software update for HomePod users. Here’s what’s new.

HomePod 27.2 adds Sound Glow, Lock Controls, Mac speaker support, and more

It’s not often that HomePod gets a software update with new features. But that’s exactly what happened today with HomePod 27.2.

The latest software update, which you can install from the Home app on your iPhone, supports four noteworthy new features:

Sound Glow

Lock Controls

Mac speaker output

Apple TV surround sound (coming soon)

Sound Glow is a new feature that turns the top of your HomePod “into a visual canvas that glows and pulses in sync with the music, reacting in real time to bass and treble.” Apple adds, “The song’s album artwork from Now Playing generates a color-matched light experience that’s unique to every song, and users can pick a soundscape like rain to trigger bespoke animations for a soothing atmosphere.”

HomePod 27.2 brings Sound Glow to HomePod (2nd generation) and HomePod mini, and it will also be supported on HomePod mini 2 later this week. You can see a hands-on in our video below:

Lock Controls is a new setting that lets you disable touch controls on the top of your HomePod. If you have a small child in your household, or perhaps a cat, this new option lets you streamline all HomePod control through your devices and voice only.

Mac speaker output lets you set one or a stereo pair of HomePods as the default audio output for your Mac. Provided you have a Mac with Wi-Fi 6E or later, you can use this new feature and never need to manually connect via AirPlay again.

Coming soon: Four-speaker surround sound with Apple TV

Finally, coming soon is a new four-speaker surround sound feature with the Apple TV 4K (4th gen), which arrives November 13. HomePod 27.2 adds support for surround sound even though users will have to wait to try it.

HomePod (2nd generation) and HomePod mini 2 are both compatible with surround sound. You can even mix-and-match large and small HomePods in your setup as long as front and rear speaker pairs match. 

Apple explains: “four speakers work together with Apple TV 4K to intelligently recognize their position in the room so audio timing and levels are automatically calibrated to the space.”

fullText:
iOS 27.2 and its corresponding updates for the HomePod lineup bring several key new features to Apple’s smart speakers. The most exciting update? The ability to finally use your HomePod as the default sound output for your Mac. This means that the 2nd-generation HomePod and HomePod mini 2 can now function as low-latency wireless speakers for your Mac!

Watch our hands-on video for an in-depth look at how the new wireless speaker functionality works, along with other new features like Sound Glow, Lock Controls, and home theater surround sound support. Be sure to subscribe to our YouTube channel for more in-depth videos.

HomePod as speakers for Mac

It’s long been possible to use a HomePod as a wireless speaker for the Mac, but doing so came with at least one big caveat: wireless latency. While it’s generally fine for movie playback, the latency is immediately noticeable when playing anything in real time. For example, playing instruments in Logic Pro, audio and FaceTime calls, etc. For these particular applications, HomePods have, up until now, been less than ideal speakers for the Mac.

Video walkthrough

Subscribe to 9to5Mac on YouTube for more videos

Apple has addressed this issue in the 27.2 update, significantly reducing latency when using a HomePod mini 2 or HomePod (2nd generation) as a wireless speaker for Mac desktops and laptops that support Wi-Fi 6E. This, unfortunately, excludes some early Apple Silicon machines, such as those powered by the M1 family of chips, but it’s good to see this feature made available.

HomePod 2nd Generation set as the Default System Output Device in System Profiler

For the HomePod mini 2, Apple included a different Wi-Fi/Bluetooth architecture based on PCIe and revised audio routing to prioritize low-latency applications. It’s also worth noting that Apple’s Wi-Fi 6E requirement applies to the Mac hardware itself and doesn’t imply that a user needs a 6E-enabled router.

HomePod 1 vs HomePod 2 latency test with Logic Pro

From that, we can gather that the update will allow the HomePod to work similarly to how it currently works with an Apple TV, when set as the default audio source. In other words, instead of relying on traditional AirPlay, it creates an ad hoc point-to-point connection between the Mac and the HomePod for minimal latency. This will make a HomePod a viable speaker-output destination for real-time audio applications.

Notice that the Play sound effects through setting now allows for AirPlay

Apple is so confident of the low-latency connection that it defaults to playing sound effects via AirPlay when a compatible HomePod is selected as the output destination. Obviously, sound effects are the sort of thing that relies on low latency, since their sound has to correspond to what is happening in the environment at that exact time; otherwise, it would be disorienting. If I select my HomePod mini (1st generation), that option is not even available.

The Play sound effects through setting doesn’t allow for AirPlay on older HomePod hardware

Needless to say, this update instantly has me reconsidering my speaker needs for my Mac desktop setup. I recently got rid of my Yamaha HS3s because I’m looking for something with a little more umph. A pair of full-sized 2nd-generation HomePods in a stereo pair would definitely fit the bill, and look much better to boot.

Lock Controls

Have you ever accidentally brushed the touch sensor on the top cap of the HomePod, activating it to play music? Do you have pets who surreptitiously activate your HomePod while you’re not in the room? If so, then the new Lock Controls switch in 27.2 will help.

When Lock Controls is enabled, the touch surface on top of the HomePod is locked, meaning touch, touch-and-hold, and volume adjustments are disabled. You’ll easily recognize when Lock Controls is enabled by the bright red “no” animation that appears.

Even the first-gen HomePod gets some love

Lock Controls will prevent a HomePod from playing audio or taking action when the device’s top cap is touched. However, intercom, alarms, timers, Check in, and FaceTime calls will continue to respond to touch.

Of all the new features in the 27.2 software update, Lock Controls is the only one that appears on all HomePod models, regardless of generation. That means that, yes, even the original OG HomePod lands support for the handy new addition!

Sound Glow

My favorite new feature in the 27.2 update is Sound Glow. This is the feature that displays ambient light that corresponds to the colors and rhythm of the album artwork for the music or podcasts being played.

Sound Glow takes full advantage of the LED Matrix displays beneath the HomePod top cap. The big HomePod features an array of 37 RGB LEDs, while the smaller HomePod mini features an array of 19 RGB LEDs. As a side note, the original HomePod features 19 LEDs across a smaller surface area than the updated version.

To enable Sound Glow, you must update your iOS device and your HomePod to 27.2. Once updated, open the Home app and venture into the settings for the HomePod you wish to adjust. There, you’ll find a Sound Glow switch you can enable. 

Apple notes that you’ll also be able to toggle Sound Glow with your voice, but it will require an Apple Intelligence‑enabled iPhone running the latest software. This could be enabled once Apple enables Siri AI on the HomePod mini 2, and perhaps the 2nd-generation HomePod, but this remains to be seen.

Home theater surround sound

If you plan to purchase an Apple TV 4K (fourth-generation), you’re likely interested in the new home theater surround sound option available with the HomePod mini 2 or the 2nd-generation full-sized HomePod. This feature lets you use four HomePods, two identical matching stereo pairs in front and rear, for a surround sound setup.

I haven’t been able to personally test this yet, because I don’t yet have the newest Apple TV 4K, but I can bet it will sound fantastic, especially when four full-sized Dolby Atmos-enabled HomePods are involved. That being said, this is an expensive proposition.

Here are the pricing details for those looking to set up a four-speaker home theater surround sound option:

Apple TV 4K ($299) + Four HomePod 2 ($349×4) = $1695

Apple TV 4K ($299) + Two HomePod 2 ($349×2) + two HomePod mini 2 ($149×2) = $1295

Apple TV 4K ($299) + Four HomePod mini 2 ($149×4) = $895

By way of comparison, Sonos’ Dolby Atmos-enabled four-speaker Immersive Set with Beam Ultra bundle can be had for less than $1600 and comes with a dedicated subwoofer. I’m not a home audio expert or an audiophile, so I can’t say which one is better, but it’s interesting that both it and the highest-tier HomePod surround setup are so similar in price.

When managing your HomePod speakers via the tvOS interface on the Apple TV 4K, you’ll see new options for Surround Sound and Whole Room Audio under the Home Theater section. The surround sound option is self-explanatory and ideal for movies and television shows, but the Whole Room Audio option is better suited to listening to music, as it provides left- and right-channel placement no matter which direction you face.

9to5Mac’s Take

iOS 27.2 provides noteworthy updates to all HomePod models, including the original HomePod, which now includes the new Lock Controls capability. But the real fun starts with the HomePod mini, with its Sound Glow support, and the HomePod mini 2 and HomePod 2nd-generation, with their support for working as the default speaker for Wi-Fi 6E-enabled Mac hardware. I think a pair of HomePod mini 2’s would look great sitting next to Apple’s just-released M6 iMac.

What do you think? Are you planning to get any of Apple’s new Home-focused hardware, or are you looking to take advantage of the new 27.2 features on hardware you already own? Sound off in the comments with your thoughts on the matter.

title: iPhone Duo tested to destruction, including removing nanotexture layer
snippet: It’s kind of wild that there’s an entire YouTube niche in which people buy the latest expensive gadgets and then find creative ways to destroy them. JerryRigEverything is one of the bigger names, and he didn’t hold back when it came to a destruction test of the iPhone Duo. In addition to subjecting the display to everything from a knife to chainmail armor, he removed the nanotexture layer and said that it kind of looks better … more…
fullText:
It’s kind of wild that there’s an entire YouTube niche in which people buy the latest expensive gadgets and then find creative ways to destroy them. JerryRigEverything is one of the bigger names, and he didn’t hold back when it came to a destruction test of the iPhone Duo.

In addition to subjecting the display to everything from a knife to chainmail armor, he removed the nanotexture layer and said that it kind of looks better … 

The first piece of bad news he discovers is that the inner display begins showing scratches at just level 2 hardness on a 10-point scale. You can even create visible grooves with a fingernail. The good news, however, is that the nano-texture display does an excellent job at hiding imperfections when the screen is on.

The iPhone scratches at a level two with deeper grooves at a level fingernail. While the screen is on, these scratches just magically disappear, just like that center crease disappears. It’s like in the construction industry. It’s very common to paint hallways and big rooms in aneggshell or satin finish instead of gloss because the non-shiny finishes hide imperfections really well. The keys and coins are leaving marks along with the medieval chainmail armor as one often has. And with the screen on, the imperfections are just totally disappearing. It’s an incredibly brilliant move on Apple’s part to have a matte display on the iPhone Duo, but when the screen turns off, those imperfections do come back.

While the iPhone Duo has a dust and waterproofing rating of IP68, theoretically meaning that it’s completely dustproof, the extreme testing used here shows that there are limits. While dust may not enter the casing, you can pour over about a beach’s worth to get enough of it trapped in the hinge mechanism that the device no longer closes.

Apple warns against removing the nanotexture layer yourself, as you can easily damage the display beneath it, but of course that didn’t stop Jerry. He found that while the display is much more reflective without it, it kind of looks better.

Yeah, the glares are back, but so are the colors. One looks like a vibrant, fresh AMOLED display, and the other looks like it has Vaseline smeared all over the top. It’s a tough trade-off, and I’m by no means telling people to take off the nanotexture layer. To be honest, you’ll probably end up breaking it, but personally, I think now it kind of looks better.

Of course, in addition to glare, the crease becomes much more visible alongside all of those scratches.

Finally, by exerting a huge amount of force to bend the hinge the wrong way, he damages the screen in the same way we’ve seen with the cracking issue in a small number of Duos.

Mostly the video is just a bit of fun, but while the dust test was certainly an extreme one, I would certainly be cautious using the Duo on a beach; best keep your chainmail armor away from it too.

title: Apple finally combined a toaster and a refrigerator
snippet: For more than 15 years, Apple has had a pretty simple answer to the idea of a touchscreen MacBook: no. Yesterday, Apple finally decided to think different and announce one anyway.
